strategy_snapshot.title: Find a novel temporal coupling, not another marker
Test a spatial or cell-composition alternative

problem:
Why can Xenopus laevis tadpoles regrow a tail at some stages, temporarily lose much of that ability, and later regain it? Investigate a specific, testable mechanism for this developmental switch; regeneration competence varies between animals.

The goal is to discover and test a previously unreported, mechanistically discriminating predictor of this switch, not to summarize known regenerative pathways or to claim all embryonic regeneration explained.

KNOWN, NOT NOVEL. A 2024 Genome Biology study identified transient regeneration-initiating cells (RICs) originating from basal epidermal cells and extracellular-matrix remodeling defects associated with regeneration failure. Other work links ROS, inflammatory and developmental signals to regeneration, and studies in X. tropicalis implicate nutritional state in stage-dependent competence. Merely identifying RICs, Wnt/BMP/FGF/ROS, ECM remodeling, or the existence of a refractory stage does NOT satisfy this project. Cross-species stage behavior is context-dependent and publications are not fully consistent; do not conflate X. tropicalis and X. laevis.

OBSERVATIONAL START. Reanalyze publicly available X. laevis regeneration/refractory transcriptomic evidence from GEO GSE245320 and its component series (bulk RNA-seq GSE245317/GSE245318, scRNA-seq GSE245312, spatial GSE245313). In the published stage-40 versus stage-46 comparison, bulk assays include 0, 0.5, 6 hours post-amputation and 3 days; verify actual samples, replicates, units and availability before analysis. scRNA-seq predominantly characterizes regenerating animals, not matched single-cell snapshots across both conditions. These datasets share a study and are NOT independent biological replications. Check later published work through the investigation date and build a cited prior-art ledger.

HYPOTHESIS SPACE. Competing mechanisms include (A) failure to induce the transient epidermal RIC/ECM-remodeling transition, (B) a stage-specific failure to couple early injury signaling to a later regenerative transcriptional program, (C) metabolic or tissue-composition gating, and (D) analytical or developmental-stage confounding. Prioritize one previously unreported *interaction, conditional dependency, or quantitative transition rule* that distinguishes at least two mechanisms, with a measurable direction, timing, tissue/cell type and uncertainty. A possible candidate is a temporal coupling between early wound-response intensity and subsequent RIC/ECM activation that differs by developmental stage; this is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.

RESEARCH METHOD. Predefine biological replicate as the unit of inference; guard against pseudoreplication (cells from the same animal/library), batch confounding, developmental-stage differences, multiple testing, cell-composition artifacts and publication reuse. Fit simple baselines (stage-only, RIC/ECM-only and known signaling modules) before proposing complexity. Quantify uncertainty and require an alternative explanation and counterfactual control. Do not invent gene-expression values, available outcome labels, intervention results, P values or accession coverage. Predictions based solely on stage class labels must not be marketed as predicting animal-level regeneration.

EXIT CRITERIA. Scientific success requires: (1) traceable evidence that the central claim is not simply already established; (2) a specified novel mechanistic prediction, including what experiment, perturbation or independent observations would falsify it; (3) a numerical effect/direction and uncertainty with appropriate baselines and negative controls; and (4) independent biological evidence on previously unseen specimens/conditions supporting the prediction. Independent replication or perturbation confirmation is required before claiming a new biological mechanism. A lower-tier COMPUTATIONAL RESULT can be reported if a previously unreported reproducible association or predictive rule outperforms preregistered known-mechanism baselines on held-out biological units with uncertainty; label it computational, exploratory and not causal. A NOVEL HYPOTHESIS can be reported with a discriminating experiment and evidence synthesis but without confirmation; do not present it as a validated scientific discovery. Otherwise exit NEGATIVE/UNRESOLVED with exact failed hypotheses, missing data and next experiment. Each strategy must deliver a bounded test and stop conditions. Avoid claiming 'solved regeneration' from any single dataset.

REFERENCES/STARTING DATA. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3 ; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE245320 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005; review https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms252111597 .

output.claim: If early and late measurements are available only from unpaired biological units, stage-stratified expression changes cannot identify an animal-level injury-to-RIC coupling rule. This is an exact identifiability limitation, not a finding about the actual GEO sample design. A specific candidate worth testing is persistence-gated epidermal signaling, but neither its novelty nor its biological effect is established here.
output.method: Separate source verification, statistical identifiability and prospective mechanism testing. No source-retrieval tool or scientific runtime is available, so accession coverage and publications cannot be inspected. First derive what unpaired time courses cannot establish. Then specify a bounded test: at comparable early epidermal injury-response intensity, persistence of that response to 3 hours should predict RIC entry at 6 hours particularly in refractory animals. A timing-controlled perturbation would distinguish persistence dependence from total signal exposure and from an operational model of a signal-insensitive RIC-entry defect. The key assumptions requiring validation are that live measurements report the intended epidermal signal without changing regeneration, and that exposure timing can be changed without changing injury severity. Positive outcomes would support this narrow dependency, not establish a complete explanation of the developmental switch. Exit for this cycle: NEGATIVE/UNRESOLVED for biological discovery; retain the exact identifiability result and an unverified candidate hypothesis.

reasoning_steps.title: Establish the evidence boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied project description attributes transient basal-epidermal RIC formation and ECM-remodeling defects to the 2024 study, and describes a stage-40 versus stage-46 comparison. These are user-supplied summaries, not inspected primary evidence. No GEO records, sample tables, article text, supplementary methods, expression matrices or specimen-level outcomes were supplied. Consequently, actual replicate counts, pooling, pairing, batches and phenotype availability remain unknown. The stated time points must not be treated as a verified sample manifest.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct a provenance-limited prior-art ledger
reasoning_steps.argument: Ledger entry 1: DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3 — project-reported evidence for RIC origin and ECM-associated failure; full text and supplements not inspected; these topics are excluded from novelty claims. Entry 2: GSE245320 and component accessions GSE245317, GSE245318, GSE245312 and GSE245313 — project-listed data sources; GSM-level contents and specimen relationships unverified; shared-study assays cannot count as independent confirmation. Entry 3: DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005 — supplied reference only; its specific findings, species and experimental scope have not been verified. Entry 4: DOI 10.3390/ijms252111597 — supplied review pointer, not inspected primary evidence. The project also identifies ROS, inflammatory/developmental signaling and nutritional influences as prior-art concerns; the stated X. tropicalis nutritional findings cannot be transferred to X. laevis. Literature coverage through 2026-11-01 is unavailable, so this ledger cannot certify novelty or completeness.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove the unpaired-data identifiability limit
reasoning_steps.argument: For a fixed stage s, define binary variables E and L denoting a prespecified high early response and later RIC entry in an animal. These are abstract variables for a proof, not invented measurements. Suppose separate samples determine p_s = P(E=1|s) and q_s = P(L=1|s). Write r_s = P(E=1,L=1|s). The four joint probabilities are r_s, p_s-r_s, q_s-r_s and 1-p_s-q_s+r_s. Nonnegativity permits every r_s in [max(0,p_s+q_s-1), min(p_s,q_s)]. All such joint distributions have identical observed marginals, while Cov(E,L|s)=r_s-p_s q_s varies across them. For nondegenerate marginals, independence and both positive and negative associations are compatible with those marginals. At a degenerate marginal, individual variation in at least one variable is absent and its coupling cannot be learned. Thus even perfectly estimated unpaired marginals do not identify within-animal coupling or its stage interaction. Pairing, an identifying model, or an intervention supplying additional information is necessary.

reasoning_steps.title: State precisely what bulk or predominantly regenerative single-cell data could establish
reasoning_steps.argument: If verified biological replicates support the design, bulk data could estimate stage-by-time differences in average module responses. That is distinct from estimating whether animals with stronger early responses later regenerate. Pool-level pairing would identify a pool-level relationship, not an individual-animal predictor. Single-cell data from predominantly regenerating animals could help define cell states or candidate readouts, but without matched refractory sampling they cannot establish a refractory-specific cell-intrinsic defect. Neither limitation proves that a coupling hypothesis is false; it limits the claim supported by those observations.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify one mechanistically discriminating candidate
reasoning_steps.argument: Candidate: refractory-stage basal epidermis is limited by persistence, rather than simply peak magnitude, of an early redox-associated injury response. Prespecify E as a baseline-corrected epidermal reporter measurement at 0.5 hours, D as the calibrated measurement at 3 hours, and L as the fraction of basal epidermal cells entering a validated RIC state at 6 hours. A candidate model is L = alpha + stage effects + beta E + gamma D + eta I(stage 46)D, with clutch effects and prespecified anatomical covariates. The directional prediction is gamma+eta > 0 and eta > 0: conditional on E, persistence is more limiting at stage 46 than at stage 40. This is an untested hypothesis, not a known result or a certified novel interaction. The added 3-hour observation is proposed, not asserted to exist in GEO. A later recovery stage must also be included prospectively before this can address regain of competence.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the bounded discriminating experiment and competing predictions
reasoning_steps.argument: Within stage and clutch, randomize animals to sham, an early supplemental epidermal redox stimulus, or a later supplemental stimulus, using matched stimulus duration and dose. Measure the actual local response rather than assuming equal delivered doses imply equal biological exposure. The proposed persistence mechanism predicts that later supplementation increases 3-hour persistence, then RIC entry and regeneration, beyond what is explained by peak response or integrated exposure. An exposure-only alternative predicts no timing advantage once those quantities are matched. An operationally signal-insensitive RIC-entry defect predicts no restoration of RIC entry despite a verified increase in persistence. Include unamputated stimulus controls, vehicle or illumination controls as applicable, wound-closure and viability measurements, and blinded scoring. A redox manipulation can have direct late effects, so rescue alone would not prove mediation through RICs; temporal ordering and an independently validated late-program blockade would be needed for that stronger inference. No delivery method, reporter or blockade is asserted to be validated here.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate measurement units, prediction and confirmation
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the animal as the prospective experimental unit; cells and image fields are subsamples. Non-destructive early, 3-hour and 6-hour measurements would be needed to associate the proposed trajectory with a blinded regeneration outcome, for example at a prespecified 7-day endpoint. If RIC measurement requires fixation, use a separate mechanistic cohort and do not claim an individual-level RIC-to-outcome relationship from it. Compare held-out-animal outcome prediction against stage-only, RIC/ECM-only and known-signaling models, using nested models with identical eligible covariates and all preprocessing confined to training data. Hold out whole clutches where feasible, block allocation across acquisition batches, and report uncertainty accounting for clutch and repeated measurements. No numerical effect, interval or performance advantage can currently be estimated. Any minimum useful effect and sample size must be fixed using an explicit precision or power calculation before confirmation, not selected after observing rescue.

reasoning_steps.title: Define falsification and stopping rules
reasoning_steps.argument: For the candidate's stated scope, evidence against it would include a precise absence of the predicted conditional persistence association, disappearance of that association after prespecified tissue-composition adjustment, or a verified persistence increase without a practically meaningful RIC or regeneration benefit. A manipulation that fails to change persistence is an unsuccessful intervention, not biological falsification. A reproducible difference between early and late stimulation that disappears after matching integrated exposure favors the exposure-only explanation. Do not expand the claim to explain later recovery without testing that developmental window. Stop before model fitting if sample provenance or biological-unit independence is unresolved; stop before a novelty claim if the exact persistence-by-stage dependency is already established in inspected prior work.

assumptions: The identifiability claim concerns the explicitly conditional case in which early and late observations provide only stage-specific marginals, without specimen pairing or an additional justified identifying model; whether the GEO data satisfy this condition is unverified.
output.evidence_status: An exact probability argument establishes a conditional identifiability limit. No primary source, GEO sample record, expression dataset or experiment was inspected; novelty, numerical effects and biological confirmation remain unresolved.
open_obligations: Obtain the GSE245320 and component-series SOFT/MINiML records, GSM annotations, supplementary-file inventories and sample-to-BioSample/library mappings. Verify species, stages, times, biological replicates, pooling, pairing, tissue boundaries, batch structure and any specimen-linked regeneration outcomes.

Inspect the full text and supplements of the supplied publications and a traceable literature search through 2026-11-01, specifically for epidermal injury-signal persistence, stage-dependent temporal coupling and timing-controlled rescue. Novelty cannot be inferred from the supplied summaries.

Validate a non-perturbing epidermal redox readout, its temporal kinetics, a RIC-state measurement and a timing-selective manipulation. Determine whether peak, integrated exposure and persistence can actually be distinguished experimentally.

Prespecify the later recovery stage, outcome rubric, minimum useful effect, sample size, clutch allocation, composition covariates, negative controls and held-out evaluation. Estimate numerical effects and uncertainty without treating cells or fields as independent animals.

Test the candidate on previously unseen X. laevis specimens and independently confirm the timing dependency. Until then, neither a novel computational result nor a new biological mechanism is established.

output.claim: Animal-level coupling between an early wound response and later regeneration cannot be identified from unpaired stage-by-time expression distributions alone. A specific candidate for prospective testing is a shortened epidermal injury-signal memory at stage 46: equal intracellular ROS exposures delivered nearer the onset of the regenerative transcriptional program should produce a larger transcriptional rescue at stage 46 than at stage 40. This is an unvalidated hypothesis, not an established novel mechanism.
output.method: First establish an exact identifiability limit rather than fit an interaction to unavailable data. Then specify a timing-versus-dose experiment that separates a temporal-transfer defect from a timing-insensitive failure of epidermal inducibility. The proposed model predicts a positive stage-by-pulse-timing interaction after matching intracellular ROS exposure; an intrinsic, timing-insensitive induction defect predicts little or no rescue from retiming alone. Biological animals are experimental units; pooled libraries, if present, are pool-level units and cannot recover individual covariance. No accession records, expression matrices, supplementary methods or later literature were available for inspection, and both execution runtimes are unavailable. Consequently, no reanalysis, sample-count verification, literature search or numerical biological estimate is claimed. The numerical threshold below is a proposed minimum effect for a future test, not an observed effect. Stop retrospective animal-level coupling analysis if samples are unpaired; stop a novelty claim if prior art already establishes the proposed dependency; stop mechanistic interpretation if exposure matching, reporter kinetics or tissue-composition controls fail.

reasoning_steps.title: Evidence boundary and provisional prior-art ledger
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied project description attributes basal-epidermal RIC origins and ECM-remodeling defects to DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3. These are treated as known background specified by the project, not independently inspected findings. GSE245320 and component accessions GSE245317/GSE245318, GSE245312 and GSE245313 are source pointers only: actual GSM records, sample counts, pooling, pairing, batches, assay units and outcome labels remain unverified. DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005 and review DOI 10.3390/ijms252111597 are additional uninspected prior-art leads; their specific claims cannot be assigned from the supplied information. No search of later publications through the investigation date was possible. Thus neither the temporal-memory rule nor its novelty is established by this ledger.

reasoning_steps.title: Exact nonidentifiability of individual temporal coupling
reasoning_steps.argument: Let X be an animal's early wound-response score and Y its later epidermal-program score. Suppose destructive sampling supplies only the distributions of X and Y in separate animals within a stage. Consider an illustrative population in which both marginals assign probability 1/2 to -1 and +1. Pairing equal signs gives E[XY]=1 and correlation +1; pairing opposite signs gives E[XY]=-1 and correlation -1. Both populations produce exactly the same observed marginals. This is a mathematical counterexample, not invented expression data. Therefore even perfect cross-sectional measurements cannot determine the sign of within-animal temporal coupling without additional assumptions or longitudinal measurements. The counterexample applies separately within each stage, so stage stratification does not fix it.

reasoning_steps.title: Why a stage-mean interaction can add no independent predictor
reasoning_steps.argument: If an early score is reduced to one mean per stage, write S=0 for stage 40 and S=1 for stage 46, and X=x40+(x46-x40)S. Then SX=x46*S, since S squared equals S. Consequently the design columns 1, S, X and SX have rank at most two: an early-response-by-stage coefficient cannot be separated from stage using only these summaries. Actual replicate-level variation could remove this algebraic rank deficiency, but unpaired replicates still do not supply individual temporal covariance. Shared-clutch trajectories could estimate a clutch-level relationship only, with independent clutches as the units.

reasoning_steps.title: A quantitative temporal-memory hypothesis
reasoning_steps.argument: Define a standardized brief injury-signal pulse at time tp after amputation, with measured intracellular basal-epidermal ROS area A. Let mu_s(tp) be the positive mean increase, relative to the matched vehicle arm, in a preregistered per-cell nascent regenerative-program output measured at 6 hpa. A candidate sub-saturating transfer model is mu_s(tp)=q_s*A*exp[-(6-tp)/tau_s]. Here q_s is stage-specific inducibility and tau_s is effective signal-memory duration; the molecular carrier is unspecified. The hypothesis is tau46<tau40, rather than merely q46<q40. This model assumes a fixed relevant readout window, comparable intracellular exposure and approximately exponential loss of effective signal. Those premises need testing; neither the 6-hour onset nor exponential kinetics is established.

reasoning_steps.title: A discriminating contrast with an exact derivation
reasoning_steps.argument: Use early and late pulses centered at 0.5 and 4 hpa. Under the candidate model, log[mu_s(4)/mu_s(0.5)]=3.5/tau_s because q_s and matched A cancel. Thus D=log[mu46(4)/mu46(0.5)]-log[mu40(4)/mu40(0.5)]=3.5*(1/tau46-1/tau40). The shortened-memory hypothesis predicts D>0. A timing-independent multiplicative loss of inducibility alone, with common tau, predicts D=0 even if stage-46 output is much lower. A proposed practically meaningful threshold is D at least log(1.5), approximately 0.405: the late/early response ratio must be at least 1.5 times larger at stage 46. This threshold is a design choice, not a measurement. The derivation also exposes limitations: if vehicle-subtracted means are nonpositive, these log ratios are undefined and this positive-response model is unsupported; they must not be rescued with arbitrary pseudocounts.

reasoning_steps.title: Bounded experiment and competing explanations
reasoning_steps.argument: After a separate feasibility pilot, freeze module genes, the readout window, dose and analysis. Randomize individual X. laevis tadpoles within stage and clutch to early pulse, late pulse, their timing-matched vehicle/sham arms, and an unmanipulated injury control. Local transient ROS exposure with washout is one candidate intervention, contingent on demonstrating acceptable toxicity and matched intracellular epidermal ROS area in the pilot. Allocation must span independent clutches and experimental days; mask image scoring and molecular analysis. Measure basal-cell number, wound closure, tissue damage and per-cell nascent transcription, rather than only bulk RNA. Include a generic acute-response readout to detect unequal pulse delivery. Estimate the stage-by-timing contrast with clutch/day structure and confidence intervals. An independent time-course cohort must test whether apparent memory loss instead reflects reporter maturation or a developmental shift in the onset of transcription. A positive D separates the proposed rule from timing-independent inducibility loss, but does not by itself distinguish shortened molecular memory from a shifted receptive window; that distinction requires directly measuring the persistence of a validated proximal signal and program onset.

reasoning_steps.title: Connect the mechanism test to individual prediction without pseudoreplication
reasoning_steps.argument: Terminal transcription measurements and later regeneration cannot be paired in the same animal without a separately validated non-destructive assay. Therefore use terminal mechanistic cohorts for the timing contrast, and a separate longitudinal cohort only after validating a live epidermal readout against nascent RNA. In the latter cohort, follow early signal, subsequent program activation and a prespecified later regeneration outcome in each animal. Compare stage-only, stage plus RIC/ECM score, and stage plus known-signaling-module baselines against one locked temporal-transfer feature. Hold out entire clutches and experimental batches, fit normalization on training data only, and report animal-level predictive uncertainty and within-stage performance. Cells and repeated images are nested observations, not additional animals. An exposure-matched perturbation effect on transcription without improved later regeneration would not establish a mechanism of regenerative competence.

reasoning_steps.title: Scope, recovery-stage test and stopping decisions
reasoning_steps.argument: Stages 40 and 46 alone cannot explain later recovery of competence. Add a prospectively selected post-refractory stage, verifying regeneration in that cohort rather than assuming its competence from stage labels. The memory hypothesis predicts that the exaggerated delay benefit should diminish as competence returns, alongside a longer measured effective signal persistence. For the proposed minimum-effect claim, an upper confidence bound for D below log(1.5) rules out the designated effect size in the tested setting; an interval spanning that threshold is inconclusive. No late-pulse rescue despite verified exposure and assay responsiveness weighs against this particular timing rule, not against all coupling mechanisms. Excess injury, unmatched intracellular exposure, or shifted assay kinetics makes the experiment mechanistically inconclusive. The contribution here is an identifiability result and a falsifiable quantitative hypothesis; novelty, biological effect size, generality and independent confirmation remain unassessed.

assumptions: The nonidentifiability result concerns unpaired early and late measurements; actual GEO pairing and sampling structure remain unknown.
The proposed biological model assumes a positive, sub-saturating transcriptional increment and comparable intracellular ROS exposure across pulse timings.
The candidate exponential memory model and 6-hour readout are hypotheses requiring pilot checks, not established properties of X. laevis.
A feasible non-destructive epidermal assay must be validated before claiming individual-level longitudinal prediction.
output.evidence_status: The identifiability limitation is established by an explicit mathematical counterexample. The temporal-memory mechanism is an unvalidated hypothesis with a numerical falsification target; no datasets, publications or specimens were inspected, and no computational or biological result is reported.
open_obligations: Inspect GEO series/GSM records, supplementary sample tables and count-matrix metadata for GSE245320 and all named components; establish animals versus pools, replicate counts, timepoints, batches, pairing, outcomes and accessible files before analysis.

Inspect the cited primary articles and review, then search subsequent work through the investigation date for injury-signal persistence, timing-dependent ROS rescue and stage-specific transfer rules; novelty cannot currently be claimed.

Verify basal-epidermal program timing, module specificity, homeolog handling, assay kinetics and composition sensitivity; identify a measurable proximal signal whose persistence could distinguish memory decay from delayed receptivity.

Pilot dose matching and safety, then obtain variance and clutch-correlation estimates for a justified sample size and preregister the confirmatory timing contrast, uncertainty calculation and stopping rules.
Acquire independent specimens, a verified recovery-stage cohort and later functional outcomes; neither scientific-success nor computational-result exit criteria have been met.

output.method: Address the unresolved reporter-kinetics obligation by exact derivation rather than unavailable computation. Test the hypothesis that two calibrated reporter values identify uninterrupted input against an alternative consisting of an early response, a signal-free gap and a late pulse. Construct inputs with exactly equal endpoint readouts, then derive their different midpoint predictions. Prospectively, distinguish the pair with a midpoint measurement after calibrating reporter decay separately within stage and injury context. Stop interpreting the reporter as persistence if independently verified washout does not follow the first-order model, calibration precision cannot resolve the predicted contrast, or intracellular input cessation cannot be verified. No scientific runtime or source-retrieval tool is available. Biological discovery remains NEGATIVE/UNRESOLVED; the contribution is an analytical constraint and a revised measurement control.

reasoning_steps.title: Scope and continuity
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied bounded extract of artifact 93746d61-5dd5-4709-9fa5-17294ac400f8 proposes epidermal signal persistence as a candidate but records reporter memory and delayed activation as unresolved alternatives. I adopt that objection and withdraw the interpretation of a 3-hour reporter value conditional on a 0.5-hour value as an identified persistence measure. The original artifact and primary biological sources were not supplied. The mathematical test below addresses the measurement part of o3/o13/o16/o20; it does not resolve their experimental-validation requirements or the remaining source, novelty and confirmation obligations.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the conditional reporter model
reasoning_steps.argument: Let t be hours after amputation and S(t) ≥ 0 the local biological input in a fixed epidermal compartment. Within stage s, assume dR/dt = k_s S(t) − λ_s R(t), with known constants k_s > 0, λ_s > 0 and R(0)=0. The observed signal is Y(t)=b_s+g_s R(t), with known baseline b_s and scale g_s>0. Calibration therefore yields R exactly in this idealized argument. Parameters may differ between stages; no stage-invariance assumption is made. The model excludes saturation, changing reporter abundance, transport, bleaching and additional kinetic states unless these have already been corrected.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive what the two readings identify
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppress the stage subscript. Multiplying the differential equation by exp(λt) and integrating gives R(t)=k∫₀ᵗ exp[−λ(t−u)]S(u)du. Consequently Q=R(3)−exp(−2.5λ)R(0.5)=k∫₀.₅³ exp[−λ(3−u)]S(u)du. Thus the second reading, after accounting for reporter carryover, identifies one positive-weighted integral of the intervening input. It does not specify when that input occurred or whether there were gaps.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct two indistinguishable nonnegative inputs
reasoning_steps.argument: Define input A by S_A(t)=1 throughout 0≤t≤3. Define input B by S_B(t)=1 on 0≤t≤0.5, S_B(t)=0 on 0.5<t<2.5, and S_B(t)=C on 2.5≤t≤3, where C=(1−exp(−2.5λ))/(1−exp(−0.5λ)). Values at individual boundary points do not affect the solution. C is finite and positive for every λ>0. The inputs coincide through 0.5 hours, so their first readings coincide. Their contributions after 0.5 hours to R(3) are respectively (k/λ)(1−exp(−2.5λ)) and (kC/λ)(1−exp(−0.5λ)), which are equal by construction. Their inherited reporter states also coincide. Hence both calibrated readings are exactly identical.

reasoning_steps.title: Show that persistence differs and derive a separating measurement
reasoning_steps.argument: For this example define persistence P as the longest uninterrupted interval in [0.5,3] on which S(t)≥1/2. Then P_A=2.5 hours and P_B=0.5 hours: B has a two-hour signal-free gap and C>1. For any 0.5<t<2.5, A has an additional constant-input contribution absent from B, giving R_A(t)−R_B(t)=(k/λ)(1−exp[−λ(t−0.5)]). In particular the 1.5-hour contrast is (k/λ)(1−exp(−λ))>0. A midpoint reading therefore separates this specified pair despite their identical endpoint readings.

reasoning_steps.title: Give an exact numerical illustration and check the boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: For an illustrative reporter with λ=ln(2) per hour and k=λ, C=(7+3√2)/4≈2.810660. Both inputs give R(0.5)=1−1/√2≈0.292893 and R(3)=7/8=0.875000. At 1.5 hours, A gives 1−1/(2√2)≈0.646447, while B gives (1−1/√2)/2≈0.146447: the exact difference is 1/2. These are algebraic model values, not expression measurements or executed simulation output. As an independent endpoint check, B carries its 0.5-hour state forward by exp(−2.5λ), then adds C(1−exp(−0.5λ)); their sum equals 1−exp(−3λ). The zero-decay limit is also nonidentifiable: with λ=0 and k>0, choosing C=5 matches the unweighted input integrals and retains the gap.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate delayed input from reporter carryover
reasoning_steps.argument: Known kinetics do rule out some explanations. Under the stated nonnegative-input model, Q=0 implies S=0 almost everywhere between 0.5 and 3 hours because the integration weight is strictly positive. Q>0 proves that some input occurred after 0.5 hours, so reporter carryover alone cannot explain it. Nevertheless Q>0 cannot distinguish sustained input from the delayed pulse constructed above. Thus kinetic calibration can exclude pure carryover without making two readings sufficient for persistence.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify stage-specific pulse–washout and midpoint controls
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed calibration: within each developmental stage and relevant wounded epidermal context, apply a bounded calibration pulse and independently verify cessation of the intracellular input at washout time t_w; removal of an external reagent alone is insufficient. With S=0 after t_w, predict R(t_w+τ)=R(t_w)exp(−λ_sτ). Multiple post-washout readings test log-linearity and estimate λ_s separately rather than imposing a common rate. If a known constant intracellular input S₀ can also be established for duration d, estimate gain from k_s=λ_s[R(t_w+d)−exp(−λ_s d)R(t_w)]/[S₀(1−exp(−λ_s d))], with t_w here denoting the start of that calibration pulse. In the injury time course, add the 1.5-hour measurement: the sustained and interrupted candidates predict a positive contrast of (k_s/λ_s)(1−exp(−λ_s)), using that stage's calibration. Include sham delivery, imaging-only, baseline-drift, viability and wound-closure controls. Randomize animals within clutch and stage, mask analysis, and propagate calibration uncertainty at the animal/clutch level rather than treating cells or frames as independent replicates. These controls are proposed, not performed or established feasible.

reasoning_steps.title: Limit the additional measurement claim
reasoning_steps.argument: One midpoint separates A and B, not all possible inputs. For any finite sampling schedule, a positive constant input within an unsampled interval can instead be replaced by a sufficiently amplified late subinterval pulse that matches its exponentially weighted contribution to the next sample. Equal reporter states at that sample then preserve every subsequent reading under identical subsequent inputs. Continuous noiseless R(t), together with valid kinetics, would recover S(t)=[dR/dt+λ_sR(t)]/k_s almost everywhere. Real differentiation amplifies measurement noise, so practical persistence inference needs a validated temporal bandwidth or rate bound, uncertainty-aware reconstruction and a stated minimum detectable gap; finite readings alone do not establish uninterrupted signaling.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied truncated peer extract 108bd13c-d94e-4d8f-8da2-5e7f52cf2958 raises biological memory versus pulse-time-dependent inducibility and exposure-matching concerns. output.claim: Under the explicitly restricted linear models below, two pulse times crossed with two post-pulse delays can distinguish shortened signal memory from pulse-time-only inducibility; an overlapping absolute readout time additionally tests readout-time-only wound-clock gating. Accumulated transcriptional output alone cannot generally distinguish memory decay from output turnover, even with an entire time course. A calibrated trajectory of the actual intervening signal, plus nascent transcription or independently calibrated output turnover, resolves that ambiguity within these restricted models. These are conditional identification results, not evidence that shortened memory causes the Xenopus laevis competence switch.
output.method: Address unresolved identification obligations o28/o30/o34 and exposure obligations o31/o35 by exact derivation, rather than fitting unavailable expression data. The biological hypothesis is that a basal-epidermal signal linking injury to regenerative transcription decays faster at stage 46 than at stage 40. Competing models place the stage difference in pulse-time inducibility, wound-clock-dependent transcriptional gain, or accumulated-output turnover. Derive their predictions on a crossed pulse/readout schedule and construct exact equivalences where discrimination fails. Replace equal ROS area with matched time-resolved, compartment-specific effective input profiles under an explicitly tested linear-response approximation. Animals are experimental units; cells and repeated images are nested measurements. No runtime, external retrieval, primary records or specimens are available, so this cycle supplies analytical model discrimination and an unperformed bounded experiment, not reanalysis, biological estimates or a novelty finding. Exit remains NEGATIVE/UNRESOLVED for the project's discovery criteria.

reasoning_steps.title: Preserve prior limitations and delimit the evidence
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied bounded extract of artifact 108bd13c-d94e-4d8f-8da2-5e7f52cf2958 contains the opposite-coupling construction for unpaired marginals and the stage-summary rank identity SX=x46 S. Both remain valid mathematical constraints, not evidence about actual GEO pairing. Its single-terminal-time memory model is a candidate, not a certified biological premise. The present derivation addresses its unresolved memory/gain and exposure ambiguities. The original artifact and the underlying GEO records/publications have not been inspected.

reasoning_steps.title: Define input, memory signal and two distinct outputs
reasoning_steps.argument: Let s denote developmental stage, p pulse onset, d elapsed time after onset, and t=p+d absolute wound age. Let u_p(t) be the perturbation-induced effective intracellular input in basal epidermis, with support p to p+w. Define the actual intervening signal P by P'=b_s u_p-k_s P, with zero incremental initial state. Let N be instantaneous nascent transcription and R an accumulated readout satisfying R'=N-lambda_s R. All quantities are perturbation-minus-time-matched-control responses under linear superposition. P, intracellular ROS input and an accumulated fluorescent reporter are not interchangeable. The derivations require positive responses, constant coefficients in the tested window, no saturation, no unmodeled feedback or hidden parallel memory, and sufficiently resolved assay calibration.

reasoning_steps.title: State the competing models and indispensable restrictions
reasoning_steps.argument: Memory model M has stage-dependent k_s and N=q_s P, with q_s independent of both pulse time and wound age. Input-gate model GI has common decay k0, but may change the encoded pulse amplitude C_s(p); after pulse termination N=q_s C_s(p) exp(-k0 d). Its gate cannot continue creating an unmeasured input after washout. Output-gate model GO has common decay k0, pulse-time-independent encoded amplitude C_s, and N=q_s g_s(t) C_s exp(-k0 d), where g_s is a function only of absolute wound age, not of pulse history. Turnover model T has common signal decay k0 and constant transcriptional gain, but stage-dependent lambda_s. These are distinct restricted alternatives. Allowing arbitrary pulse-history dependence, hidden states, or simultaneous unrestricted encoding and output gates removes the intended identification.

reasoning_steps.title: A crossed schedule with an informative shared wound age
reasoning_steps.argument: Choose p2-p1=d2-d1=L>0 and d1>w. Then t12=p1+d2 equals t21=p2+d1. One illustrative schedule retaining the previous pulse times is p1=0.5, p2=4, d1=2 and d2=5.5 hours: the four readouts occur at 2.5, 6, 6 and 9.5 hpa. These are design values, not verified biological windows. Each animal receives only its assigned pulse; terminal assays use separate randomized animals for each cell of the design. Under matched translated inputs, integration gives P_s(p+d)=C_s exp(-k_s d), where C_s=b_s integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv. The same C_s applies to both pulse times within stage only if input profiles and encoding gain satisfy the stated restrictions.

reasoning_steps.title: Distinguish memory from the original pulse-time-gain alternative
reasoning_steps.argument: Write N_sij=N_s(p_i+d_j). Under M, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k_s L for either pulse time, and N_s2j/N_s1j=1 at either common delay. Under GI, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k0 L, while N_s2j/N_s1j=C_s(p2)/C_s(p1). Thus GI can mimic a stage-dependent late/early pulse response at one terminal time but cannot mimic unequal stage-specific delay slopes over the crossed design when its post-pulse memory is common. This follows by cancellation of pulse-specific amplitudes within each pulse arm. Equal k_s, constant input gates or insufficient precision are nondiscriminating cases, not evidence favoring one mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: Distinguish output-clock gating and explain why overlap matters
reasoning_steps.argument: Under GO, N_sij=q_s C_s g_s(p_i+d_j) exp(-k0 d_j). If all four absolute times are distinct, an unrestricted positive g_s can interpolate the four values required to mimic M; crossing alone is insufficient. At the shared time t12=t21, however, g_s cancels: K_s=log(N_s21/N_s12)/L=k0. Under M, K_s=k_s. Consequently K46-K40>0 is predicted by shortened stage-46 memory, whereas GO with common memory predicts zero. A pulse-time encoding gate does not cancel at this shared time, which is why the within-pulse delay contrasts from the previous step are also needed. The overlap result requires equal encoded amplitudes across pulse times under GO.

reasoning_steps.title: Exhibit the remaining unrestricted-gating equivalence
reasoning_steps.argument: Even the crossed design is not a universal identification theorem. For impulse responses, a common-memory model N=a_s(p)g_s(t) exp(-k0 d) reproduces M exactly by choosing a_s(p)=q_s C_s exp[(k_s-k0)p] and g_s(t)=exp[-(k_s-k0)t]. Their product is q_s C_s exp(-k_s d). This equality holds for every p and d, not merely four measurements. Therefore output-only observations cannot exclude combined encoding and wound-clock gates. Measuring the actual causal P, rather than an upstream correlate, supplies an additional restriction: common-memory alternatives predict a common normalized post-pulse P decay, whereas M predicts stage-specific decay. Without validating that P is the relevant intervening state, this broader biological ambiguity remains.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove the memory-versus-turnover ambiguity
reasoning_steps.argument: For an ideal impulse producing P=C exp(-k d), zero initial R and N=qP, integration gives R(d)=qC[exp(-k d)-exp(-lambda d)]/(lambda-k). At lambda=k the continuous limit is qC d exp(-k d). The expression is invariant under exchanging k and lambda. More generally, for any finite input the zero-state response is bq times the convolution of u, exp(-k t) and exp(-lambda t); convolution commutes. Thus a model with stage-dependent k_s and common lambda0 has exactly the same R as a model with common k0=lambda0 and stage-dependent lambda_s=k_s, with matched gain products. No number of accumulated-output observations alone breaks this equivalence under these linear models.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify what a validated proximal trajectory actually identifies
reasoning_steps.argument: After verified washout, a calibrated P trajectory identifies k_s from -d log(P)/dt, independent of a constant unknown amplitude. M requires the same within-stage decay for both pulse times, faster decay at stage 46, and constant N/P=q_s across wound ages. GI permits pulse-amplitude differences but requires common normalized decay. GO requires common normalized decay and N/P varying only with wound age. T requires common P decay and constant N/P; its apparent output persistence differs through lambda_s. Direct nascent N avoids accumulated-output turnover. Alternatively, with independently measured lambda_s and adequately resolved R, N=R'+lambda_s R. Four accumulated-output endpoints do not supply a nonparametric derivative or calibrate arbitrary reporter kinetics. A sensor trajectory with unknown stage-dependent filtering is not a validated P trajectory.

reasoning_steps.title: Replace ROS-area matching with the required profile control
reasoning_steps.argument: The effective post-pulse signal is b_s exp(-k_s d) integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv, not a function of unweighted area alone. For an exact finite-pulse counterexample, give both inputs area A: u1=A/epsilon on [0,epsilon] and u2=A/epsilon on [w-epsilon,w], with 0<epsilon<w. Their weighted integrals differ by exp[k_s(w-epsilon)], despite equal area. The appropriate robust control is the same translated intracellular effective-input profile u_s,i(p_i+v,x)=u*(v,x), including amplitude, duration, rise/fall shape and relevant subcellular localization x. This matches the input, not the downstream P tail whose decay is being tested. Increment matching is sufficient only after testing additive superposition against endogenous injury signaling; otherwise relevant total input and initial-state differences must be controlled or explicitly modeled.

reasoning_steps.title: Bound profile mismatch and define the falsification contrast
reasoning_steps.argument: For a nonnegative kernel, if each achieved input lies pointwise between (1-epsilon)u* and (1+epsilon)u*, its linear response satisfies the same relative bounds. A log ratio of two responses can therefore be displaced by at most log[(1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon)], and a difference of two such log ratios by at most twice that amount. This is a theoretical tolerance bound, not measured uncertainty. At the shared wound age define D=log(N_46,21/N_46,12)-log(N_40,21/N_40,12). M gives D=L(k46-k40); GO and constant-gain common-memory T give D=0. GI may give positive D, but predicts common delay slopes. The previously proposed D≥log(1.5), approximately 0.405, remains only a minimum-effect design target. Nonpositive control-subtracted means invalidate these log contrasts; no pseudocount rescue is justified.

reasoning_steps.title: Bound the next biological test and its stopping rules
reasoning_steps.argument: First perform a separate feasibility pilot to validate a nonperturbing basal-epidermal input sensor, the candidate P assay, intracellular washout, nascent-transcription timing and any accumulated-readout turnover. Freeze the pulse protocol, profile tolerances and one primary contrast before confirmation. Randomize animals within stage and clutch across the four pulse/delay cells, timing-matched vehicles, sham delivery and injury-only controls; distribute allocation across days and mask scoring. Measure cell counts, tissue damage and wound closure to detect composition or toxicity effects. Estimate contrasts using animals as units and clutch/day structure, with simultaneous uncertainty for the small prespecified contrast family. Stop as mechanistically inconclusive if profile control, washout, assay calibration or model restrictions fail. Reject the designated minimum-effect version if its uncertainty upper bound falls below the threshold after exposure uncertainty is incorporated. Common P decay with valid measurement contradicts this specified P-memory hypothesis, not every possible hidden-memory mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: Assess peer extracts, novelty and the developmental scope
reasoning_steps.argument: Peer extracts 93746d61-5dd5-4709-9fa5-17294ac400f8 and a4378486-799b-4acd-9991-15fbf7e443f5 raise input matching and reporter-memory ambiguities; fc219f96-452e-4d88-be65-8983613199be records a source-readiness stop. These are unverified, partly truncated extracts, not inspected originals or independent confirmations. I adopt their calibration concerns as design constraints, not their unsupplied results as premises. They do not refute this restricted derivation. The proposed biological extension is that a verified post-refractory competent cohort should recover longer P persistence and reduced timing sensitivity; that is an additional conjecture, not entailed by comparing stages 40 and 46. No transfer from X. tropicalis is made. Novelty, animal-level prediction and functional relevance remain unassessed.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove the unpaired-data identifiability limit
reasoning_steps.argument: For a fixed stage s, define binary variables E and L denoting a prespecified high early response and later RIC entry in an animal. These are abstract variables for a proof, not invented measurements. Suppose separate samples determine p_s = P(E=1|s) and q_s = P(L=1|s). Write r_s = P(E=1,L=1|s). The four joint probabilities are r_s, p_s-r_s, q_s-r_s and 1-p_s-q_s+r_s. Nonnegativity permits every r_s in [max(0,p_s+q_s-1), min(p_s,q_s)]. All such joint distributions have identical observed marginals, while Cov(E,L|s)=r_s-p_s q_s varies across them. For nondegenerate marginals, independence and both positive and negative associations are compatible with those marginals. At a degenerate marginal, individual variation in at least one variable is absent and its coupling cannot be learned. Thus even perfectly estimated unpaired marginals do not identify within-animal coupling or its stage interaction. Pairing, an identifying model, or an intervention supplying additional information is necessary.

reasoning_steps.title: State precisely what bulk or predominantly regenerative single-cell data could establish
reasoning_steps.argument: If verified biological replicates support the design, bulk data could estimate stage-by-time differences in average module responses. That is distinct from estimating whether animals with stronger early responses later regenerate. Pool-level pairing would identify a pool-level relationship, not an individual-animal predictor. Single-cell data from predominantly regenerating animals could help define cell states or candidate readouts, but without matched refractory sampling they cannot establish a refractory-specific cell-intrinsic defect. Neither limitation proves that a coupling hypothesis is false; it limits the claim supported by those observations.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify one mechanistically discriminating candidate
reasoning_steps.argument: Candidate: refractory-stage basal epidermis is limited by persistence, rather than simply peak magnitude, of an early redox-associated injury response. Prespecify E as a baseline-corrected epidermal reporter measurement at 0.5 hours, D as the calibrated measurement at 3 hours, and L as the fraction of basal epidermal cells entering a validated RIC state at 6 hours. A candidate model is L = alpha + stage effects + beta E + gamma D + eta I(stage 46)D, with clutch effects and prespecified anatomical covariates. The directional prediction is gamma+eta > 0 and eta > 0: conditional on E, persistence is more limiting at stage 46 than at stage 40. This is an untested hypothesis, not a known result or a certified novel interaction. The added 3-hour observation is proposed, not asserted to exist in GEO. A later recovery stage must also be included prospectively before this can address regain of competence.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the bounded discriminating experiment and competing predictions
reasoning_steps.argument: Within stage and clutch, randomize animals to sham, an early supplemental epidermal redox stimulus, or a later supplemental stimulus, using matched stimulus duration and dose. Measure the actual local response rather than assuming equal delivered doses imply equal biological exposure. The proposed persistence mechanism predicts that later supplementation increases 3-hour persistence, then RIC entry and regeneration, beyond what is explained by peak response or integrated exposure. An exposure-only alternative predicts no timing advantage once those quantities are matched. An operationally signal-insensitive RIC-entry defect predicts no restoration of RIC entry despite a verified increase in persistence. Include unamputated stimulus controls, vehicle or illumination controls as applicable, wound-closure and viability measurements, and blinded scoring. A redox manipulation can have direct late effects, so rescue alone would not prove mediation through RICs; temporal ordering and an independently validated late-program blockade would be needed for that stronger inference. No delivery method, reporter or blockade is asserted to be validated here.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate measurement units, prediction and confirmation
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the animal as the prospective experimental unit; cells and image fields are subsamples. Non-destructive early, 3-hour and 6-hour measurements would be needed to associate the proposed trajectory with a blinded regeneration outcome, for example at a prespecified 7-day endpoint. If RIC measurement requires fixation, use a separate mechanistic cohort and do not claim an individual-level RIC-to-outcome relationship from it. Compare held-out-animal outcome prediction against stage-only, RIC/ECM-only and known-signaling models, using nested models with identical eligible covariates and all preprocessing confined to training data. Hold out whole clutches where feasible, block allocation across acquisition batches, and report uncertainty accounting for clutch and repeated measurements. No numerical effect, interval or performance advantage can currently be estimated. Any minimum useful effect and sample size must be fixed using an explicit precision or power calculation before confirmation, not selected after observing rescue.

reasoning_steps.title: Define falsification and stopping rules
reasoning_steps.argument: For the candidate's stated scope, evidence against it would include a precise absence of the predicted conditional persistence association, disappearance of that association after prespecified tissue-composition adjustment, or a verified persistence increase without a practically meaningful RIC or regeneration benefit. A manipulation that fails to change persistence is an unsuccessful intervention, not biological falsification. A reproducible difference between early and late stimulation that disappears after matching integrated exposure favors the exposure-only explanation. Do not expand the claim to explain later recovery without testing that developmental window. Stop before model fitting if sample provenance or biological-unit independence is unresolved; stop before a novelty claim if the exact persistence-by-stage dependency is already established in inspected prior work.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied project description attributes basal-epidermal RIC origins and ECM-remodeling defects to DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3. These are treated as known background specified by the project, not independently inspected findings. GSE245320 and component accessions GSE245317/GSE245318, GSE245312 and GSE245313 are source pointers only: actual GSM records, sample counts, pooling, pairing, batches, assay units and outcome labels remain unverified. reasoning_steps.title: Exact nonidentifiability of individual temporal coupling
reasoning_steps.argument: Let X be an animal's early wound-response score and Y its later epidermal-program score. Suppose destructive sampling supplies only the distributions of X and Y in separate animals within a stage. Consider an illustrative population in which both marginals assign probability 1/2 to -1 and +1. Pairing equal signs gives E[XY]=1 and correlation +1; pairing opposite signs gives E[XY]=-1 and correlation -1. Both populations produce exactly the same observed marginals. This is a mathematical counterexample, not invented expression data. Therefore even perfect cross-sectional measurements cannot determine the sign of within-animal temporal coupling without additional assumptions or longitudinal measurements. The counterexample applies separately within each stage, so stage stratification does not fix it.

reasoning_steps.title: Why a stage-mean interaction can add no independent predictor
reasoning_steps.argument: If an early score is reduced to one mean per stage, write S=0 for stage 40 and S=1 for stage 46, and X=x40+(x46-x40)S. Then SX=x46*S, since S squared equals S. Consequently the design columns 1, S, X and SX have rank at most two: an early-response-by-stage coefficient cannot be separated from stage using only these summaries. Actual replicate-level variation could remove this algebraic rank deficiency, but unpaired replicates still do not supply individual temporal covariance. Shared-clutch trajectories could estimate a clutch-level relationship only, with independent clutches as the units.

reasoning_steps.title: A quantitative temporal-memory hypothesis
reasoning_steps.argument: Define a standardized brief injury-signal pulse at time tp after amputation, with measured intracellular basal-epidermal ROS area A. Let mu_s(tp) be the positive mean increase, relative to the matched vehicle arm, in a preregistered per-cell nascent regenerative-program output measured at 6 hpa. A candidate sub-saturating transfer model is mu_s(tp)=q_s*A*exp[-(6-tp)/tau_s]. Here q_s is stage-specific inducibility and tau_s is effective signal-memory duration; the molecular carrier is unspecified. The hypothesis is tau46<tau40, rather than merely q46<q40. This model assumes a fixed relevant readout window, comparable intracellular exposure and approximately exponential loss of effective signal. Those premises need testing; neither the 6-hour onset nor exponential kinetics is established.

reasoning_steps.title: A discriminating contrast with an exact derivation
reasoning_steps.argument: Use early and late pulses centered at 0.5 and 4 hpa. Under the candidate model, log[mu_s(4)/mu_s(0.5)]=3.5/tau_s because q_s and matched A cancel. Thus D=log[mu46(4)/mu46(0.5)]-log[mu40(4)/mu40(0.5)]=3.5*(1/tau46-1/tau40). The shortened-memory hypothesis predicts D>0. A timing-independent multiplicative loss of inducibility alone, with common tau, predicts D=0 even if stage-46 output is much lower. A proposed practically meaningful threshold is D at least log(1.5), approximately 0.405: the late/early response ratio must be at least 1.5 times larger at stage 46. This threshold is a design choice, not a measurement. The derivation also exposes limitations: if vehicle-subtracted means are nonpositive, these log ratios are undefined and this positive-response model is unsupported; they must not be rescued with arbitrary pseudocounts.

reasoning_steps.title: Bounded experiment and competing explanations
reasoning_steps.argument: After a separate feasibility pilot, freeze module genes, the readout window, dose and analysis. Randomize individual X. laevis tadpoles within stage and clutch to early pulse, late pulse, their timing-matched vehicle/sham arms, and an unmanipulated injury control. Local transient ROS exposure with washout is one candidate intervention, contingent on demonstrating acceptable toxicity and matched intracellular epidermal ROS area in the pilot. Allocation must span independent clutches and experimental days; mask image scoring and molecular analysis. Measure basal-cell number, wound closure, tissue damage and per-cell nascent transcription, rather than only bulk RNA. Include a generic acute-response readout to detect unequal pulse delivery. Estimate the stage-by-timing contrast with clutch/day structure and confidence intervals. An independent time-course cohort must test whether apparent memory loss instead reflects reporter maturation or a developmental shift in the onset of transcription. A positive D separates the proposed rule from timing-independent inducibility loss, but does not by itself distinguish shortened molecular memory from a shifted receptive window; that distinction requires directly measuring the persistence of a validated proximal signal and program onset.

reasoning_steps.title: Connect the mechanism test to individual prediction without pseudoreplication
reasoning_steps.argument: Terminal transcription measurements and later regeneration cannot be paired in the same animal without a separately validated non-destructive assay. Therefore use terminal mechanistic cohorts for the timing contrast, and a separate longitudinal cohort only after validating a live epidermal readout against nascent RNA. In the latter cohort, follow early signal, subsequent program activation and a prespecified later regeneration outcome in each animal. Compare stage-only, stage plus RIC/ECM score, and stage plus known-signaling-module baselines against one locked temporal-transfer feature. Hold out entire clutches and experimental batches, fit normalization on training data only, and report animal-level predictive uncertainty and within-stage performance. Cells and repeated images are nested observations, not additional animals. An exposure-matched perturbation effect on transcription without improved later regeneration would not establish a mechanism of regenerative competence.

reasoning_steps.title: Scope, recovery-stage test and stopping decisions
reasoning_steps.argument: Stages 40 and 46 alone cannot explain later recovery of competence. Add a prospectively selected post-refractory stage, verifying regeneration in that cohort rather than assuming its competence from stage labels. reasoning_steps.title: Exact nonidentifiability of individual temporal coupling
reasoning_steps.argument: Let X be an animal's early wound-response score and Y its later epidermal-program score. Suppose destructive sampling supplies only the distributions of X and Y in separate animals within a stage. Consider an illustrative population in which both marginals assign probability 1/2 to -1 and +1. Pairing equal signs gives E[XY]=1 and correlation +1; pairing opposite signs gives E[XY]=-1 and correlation -1. Both populations produce exactly the same observed marginals. This is a mathematical counterexample, not invented expression data. Therefore even perfect cross-sectional measurements cannot determine the sign of within-animal temporal coupling without additional assumptions or longitudinal measurements. The counterexample applies separately within each stage, so stage stratification does not fix it.

review.rationale: Both constructed joint distributions have equal ±1 marginals, zero marginal means, and unit variances, while E[XY] is respectively +1 and −1. This proves nonidentifiability from unpaired marginals, separately within either stage.

reasoning_steps.title: Why a stage-mean interaction can add no independent predictor
reasoning_steps.argument: If an early score is reduced to one mean per stage, write S=0 for stage 40 and S=1 for stage 46, and X=x40+(x46-x40)S. Then SX=x46*S, since S squared equals S. Consequently the design columns 1, S, X and SX have rank at most two: an early-response-by-stage coefficient cannot be separated from stage using only these summaries. Actual replicate-level variation could remove this algebraic rank deficiency, but unpaired replicates still do not supply individual temporal covariance. Shared-clutch trajectories could estimate a clutch-level relationship only, with independent clutches as the units.

review.rationale: With binary S, X lies in the span of 1 and S and SX=x46S. Therefore all four columns lie in a two-dimensional span. The distinction between individual, pool, and clutch-level associations is correctly maintained.

reasoning_steps.title: A quantitative temporal-memory hypothesis
reasoning_steps.argument: Define a standardized brief injury-signal pulse at time tp after amputation, with measured intracellular basal-epidermal ROS area A. Let mu_s(tp) be the positive mean increase, relative to the matched vehicle arm, in a preregistered per-cell nascent regenerative-program output measured at 6 hpa. A candidate sub-saturating transfer model is mu_s(tp)=q_s*A*exp[-(6-tp)/tau_s]. Here q_s is stage-specific inducibility and tau_s is effective signal-memory duration; the molecular carrier is unspecified. The hypothesis is tau46<tau40, rather than merely q46<q40. This model assumes a fixed relevant readout window, comparable intracellular exposure and approximately exponential loss of effective signal. Those premises need testing; neither the 6-hour onset nor exponential kinetics is established.

review.rationale: The equation defines a coherent candidate impulse-response model with explicit positivity and sub-saturation requirements; it does not establish those properties biologically.
review.objection: Neither exponential persistence, constant inducibility across pulse times, the relevant six-hour window, nor effective exposure matching is supported by inspected evidence. Equal exposure area is insufficient for finite pulses unless their relevant profiles are also controlled.

reasoning_steps.title: A discriminating contrast with an exact derivation
reasoning_steps.argument: Use early and late pulses centered at 0.5 and 4 hpa. Under the candidate model, log[mu_s(4)/mu_s(0.5)]=3.5/tau_s because q_s and matched A cancel. Thus D=log[mu46(4)/mu46(0.5)]-log[mu40(4)/mu40(0.5)]=3.5*(1/tau46-1/tau40). The shortened-memory hypothesis predicts D>0. A timing-independent multiplicative loss of inducibility alone, with common tau, predicts D=0 even if stage-46 output is much lower. A proposed practically meaningful threshold is D at least log(1.5), approximately 0.405: the late/early response ratio must be at least 1.5 times larger at stage 46. This threshold is a design choice, not a measurement. The derivation also exposes limitations: if vehicle-subtracted means are nonpositive, these log ratios are undefined and this positive-response model is unsupported; they must not be rescued with arbitrary pseudocounts.

review.rationale: As an internal calculation within the proposed model, cancellation of positive q_s and equal A gives log[mu_s(4)/mu_s(0.5)]=3.5/tau_s and the stated D. The threshold and undefined-log limitation are accurately distinguished from observations.

Allocation must span independent clutches and experimental days; mask image scoring and molecular analysis. An independent time-course cohort must test whether apparent memory loss instead reflects reporter maturation or a developmental shift in the onset of transcription. A positive D separates the proposed rule from timing-independent inducibility loss, but does not by itself distinguish shortened molecular memory from a shifted receptive window; that distinction requires directly measuring the persistence of a validated proximal signal and program onset.

reasoning_steps.title: Connect the mechanism test to individual prediction without pseudoreplication
reasoning_steps.argument: Terminal transcription measurements and later regeneration cannot be paired in the same animal without a separately validated non-destructive assay. reasoning_steps.title: Scope and continuity
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied bounded extract of artifact 93746d61-5dd5-4709-9fa5-17294ac400f8 proposes epidermal signal persistence as a candidate but records reporter memory and delayed activation as unresolved alternatives. I adopt that objection and withdraw the interpretation of a 3-hour reporter value conditional on a 0.5-hour value as an identified persistence measure. The original artifact and primary biological sources were not supplied. The mathematical test below addresses the measurement part of o3/o13/o16/o20; it does not resolve their experimental-validation requirements or the remaining source, novelty and confirmation obligations.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the conditional reporter model
reasoning_steps.argument: Let t be hours after amputation and S(t) ≥ 0 the local biological input in a fixed epidermal compartment. Within stage s, assume dR/dt = k_s S(t) − λ_s R(t), with known constants k_s > 0, λ_s > 0 and R(0)=0. The observed signal is Y(t)=b_s+g_s R(t), with known baseline b_s and scale g_s>0. Calibration therefore yields R exactly in this idealized argument. Parameters may differ between stages; no stage-invariance assumption is made. The model excludes saturation, changing reporter abundance, transport, bleaching and additional kinetic states unless these have already been corrected.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive what the two readings identify
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppress the stage subscript. Multiplying the differential equation by exp(λt) and integrating gives R(t)=k∫₀ᵗ exp[−λ(t−u)]S(u)du. Consequently Q=R(3)−exp(−2.5λ)R(0.5)=k∫₀.₅³ exp[−λ(3−u)]S(u)du. Thus the second reading, after accounting for reporter carryover, identifies one positive-weighted integral of the intervening input. It does not specify when that input occurred or whether there were gaps.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct two indistinguishable nonnegative inputs
reasoning_steps.argument: Define input A by S_A(t)=1 throughout 0≤t≤3. Define input B by S_B(t)=1 on 0≤t≤0.5, S_B(t)=0 on 0.5<t<2.5, and S_B(t)=C on 2.5≤t≤3, where C=(1−exp(−2.5λ))/(1−exp(−0.5λ)). Values at individual boundary points do not affect the solution. C is finite and positive for every λ>0. The inputs coincide through 0.5 hours, so their first readings coincide. Their contributions after 0.5 hours to R(3) are respectively (k/λ)(1−exp(−2.5λ)) and (kC/λ)(1−exp(−0.5λ)), which are equal by construction. Their inherited reporter states also coincide. Hence both calibrated readings are exactly identical.

reasoning_steps.title: Show that persistence differs and derive a separating measurement
reasoning_steps.argument: For this example define persistence P as the longest uninterrupted interval in [0.5,3] on which S(t)≥1/2. Then P_A=2.5 hours and P_B=0.5 hours: B has a two-hour signal-free gap and C>1. For any 0.5<t<2.5, A has an additional constant-input contribution absent from B, giving R_A(t)−R_B(t)=(k/λ)(1−exp[−λ(t−0.5)]). In particular the 1.5-hour contrast is (k/λ)(1−exp(−λ))>0. A midpoint reading therefore separates this specified pair despite their identical endpoint readings.

reasoning_steps.title: Give an exact numerical illustration and check the boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: For an illustrative reporter with λ=ln(2) per hour and k=λ, C=(7+3√2)/4≈2.810660. Both inputs give R(0.5)=1−1/√2≈0.292893 and R(3)=7/8=0.875000. At 1.5 hours, A gives 1−1/(2√2)≈0.646447, while B gives (1−1/√2)/2≈0.146447: the exact difference is 1/2. These are algebraic model values, not expression measurements or executed simulation output. As an independent endpoint check, B carries its 0.5-hour state forward by exp(−2.5λ), then adds C(1−exp(−0.5λ)); their sum equals 1−exp(−3λ). The zero-decay limit is also nonidentifiable: with λ=0 and k>0, choosing C=5 matches the unweighted input integrals and retains the gap.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate delayed input from reporter carryover
reasoning_steps.argument: Known kinetics do rule out some explanations. Under the stated nonnegative-input model, Q=0 implies S=0 almost everywhere between 0.5 and 3 hours because the integration weight is strictly positive. Q>0 proves that some input occurred after 0.5 hours, so reporter carryover alone cannot explain it. Nevertheless Q>0 cannot distinguish sustained input from the delayed pulse constructed above. Thus kinetic calibration can exclude pure carryover without making two readings sufficient for persistence.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify stage-specific pulse–washout and midpoint controls
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed calibration: within each developmental stage and relevant wounded epidermal context, apply a bounded calibration pulse and independently verify cessation of the intracellular input at washout time t_w; removal of an external reagent alone is insufficient. With S=0 after t_w, predict R(t_w+τ)=R(t_w)exp(−λ_sτ). Multiple post-washout readings test log-linearity and estimate λ_s separately rather than imposing a common rate. If a known constant intracellular input S₀ can also be established for duration d, estimate gain from k_s=λ_s[R(t_w+d)−exp(−λ_s d)R(t_w)]/[S₀(1−exp(−λ_s d))], with t_w here denoting the start of that calibration pulse. In the injury time course, add the 1.5-hour measurement: the sustained and interrupted candidates predict a positive contrast of (k_s/λ_s)(1−exp(−λ_s)), using that stage's calibration. Include sham delivery, imaging-only, baseline-drift, viability and wound-closure controls. Randomize animals within clutch and stage, mask analysis, and propagate calibration uncertainty at the animal/clutch level rather than treating cells or frames as independent replicates. These controls are proposed, not performed or established feasible.

reasoning_steps.title: Limit the additional measurement claim
reasoning_steps.argument: One midpoint separates A and B, not all possible inputs. For any finite sampling schedule, a positive constant input within an unsampled interval can instead be replaced by a sufficiently amplified late subinterval pulse that matches its exponentially weighted contribution to the next sample. Equal reporter states at that sample then preserve every subsequent reading under identical subsequent inputs. Continuous noiseless R(t), together with valid kinetics, would recover S(t)=[dR/dt+λ_sR(t)]/k_s almost everywhere. Real differentiation amplifies measurement noise, so practical persistence inference needs a validated temporal bandwidth or rate bound, uncertainty-aware reconstruction and a stated minimum detectable gap; finite readings alone do not establish uninterrupted signaling.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied truncated peer extract 108bd13c-d94e-4d8f-8da2-5e7f52cf2958 raises biological memory versus pulse-time-dependent inducibility and exposure-matching concerns. A validated temporal readout would still leave unresolved whether signal persistence causes RIC entry, whether the interaction is previously unreported, and whether it explains later recovery of competence in X. laevis.
