reasoning_steps.title: Define the conditional reporter model
reasoning_steps.argument: Let t be hours after amputation and S(t) ≥ 0 the local biological input in a fixed epidermal compartment. Within stage s, assume dR/dt = k_s S(t) − λ_s R(t), with known constants k_s > 0, λ_s > 0 and R(0)=0. The observed signal is Y(t)=b_s+g_s R(t), with known baseline b_s and scale g_s>0. Calibration therefore yields R exactly in this idealized argument. Parameters may differ between stages; no stage-invariance assumption is made. The model excludes saturation, changing reporter abundance, transport, bleaching and additional kinetic states unless these have already been corrected.

review.rationale: This is an explicit premise, not an established reporter property. It matches the conditional claim and allows different parameters across stages while specifying the initial state and observation map needed for the derivation.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive what the two readings identify
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppress the stage subscript. Multiplying the differential equation by exp(λt) and integrating gives R(t)=k∫₀ᵗ exp[−λ(t−u)]S(u)du. Consequently Q=R(3)−exp(−2.5λ)R(0.5)=k∫₀.₅³ exp[−λ(3−u)]S(u)du. Thus the second reading, after accounting for reporter carryover, identifies one positive-weighted integral of the intervening input. It does not specify when that input occurred or whether there were gaps.

review.rationale: Applying the integrating factor and subtracting the propagated 0.5-hour state gives exactly the stated weighted integral over 0.5–3 hours. One such integral does not generally locate its contributing input in time.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct two indistinguishable nonnegative inputs
reasoning_steps.argument: Define input A by S_A(t)=1 throughout 0≤t≤3. Define input B by S_B(t)=1 on 0≤t≤0.5, S_B(t)=0 on 0.5<t<2.5, and S_B(t)=C on 2.5≤t≤3, where C=(1−exp(−2.5λ))/(1−exp(−0.5λ)). Values at individual boundary points do not affect the solution. C is finite and positive for every λ>0. The inputs coincide through 0.5 hours, so their first readings coincide. Their contributions after 0.5 hours to R(3) are respectively (k/λ)(1−exp(−2.5λ)) and (kC/λ)(1−exp(−0.5λ)), which are equal by construction. Their inherited reporter states also coincide. Hence both calibrated readings are exactly identical.

review.rationale: The trajectories coincide before the first reading. The chosen positive finite C equates their subsequent weighted contributions, and their inherited states are equal, proving exact endpoint equality.

reasoning_steps.title: Show that persistence differs and derive a separating measurement
reasoning_steps.argument: For this example define persistence P as the longest uninterrupted interval in [0.5,3] on which S(t)≥1/2. Then P_A=2.5 hours and P_B=0.5 hours: B has a two-hour signal-free gap and C>1. For any 0.5<t<2.5, A has an additional constant-input contribution absent from B, giving R_A(t)−R_B(t)=(k/λ)(1−exp[−λ(t−0.5)]). In particular the 1.5-hour contrast is (k/λ)(1−exp(−λ))>0. A midpoint reading therefore separates this specified pair despite their identical endpoint readings.

review.rationale: Because C>1, the threshold-defined persistence is 2.5 hours for A and 0.5 hours for B. Before the late pulse, subtracting the two state equations gives the stated strictly positive contrast, including at 1.5 hours.

reasoning_steps.title: Give an exact numerical illustration and check the boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: For an illustrative reporter with λ=ln(2) per hour and k=λ, C=(7+3√2)/4≈2.810660. Both inputs give R(0.5)=1−1/√2≈0.292893 and R(3)=7/8=0.875000. At 1.5 hours, A gives 1−1/(2√2)≈0.646447, while B gives (1−1/√2)/2≈0.146447: the exact difference is 1/2. These are algebraic model values, not expression measurements or executed simulation output. As an independent endpoint check, B carries its 0.5-hour state forward by exp(−2.5λ), then adds C(1−exp(−0.5λ)); their sum equals 1−exp(−3λ). The zero-decay limit is also nonidentifiable: with λ=0 and k>0, choosing C=5 matches the unweighted input integrals and retains the gap.

review.rationale: Substitution of λ=ln(2) and k=λ yields the stated radical amplitude, common endpoint values and exact midpoint difference of 1/2. The λ=0 boundary example also follows by matching unweighted input integrals. These are algebraic illustrations, not execution results.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate delayed input from reporter carryover
reasoning_steps.argument: Known kinetics do rule out some explanations. Under the stated nonnegative-input model, Q=0 implies S=0 almost everywhere between 0.5 and 3 hours because the integration weight is strictly positive. Q>0 proves that some input occurred after 0.5 hours, so reporter carryover alone cannot explain it. Nevertheless Q>0 cannot distinguish sustained input from the delayed pulse constructed above. Thus kinetic calibration can exclude pure carryover without making two readings sufficient for persistence.

review.rationale: For nonnegative input and a strictly positive kernel, a zero integral implies zero input almost everywhere. Positive Q therefore excludes pure carryover under the model, but does not distinguish sustained input from a delayed contribution.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify stage-specific pulse–washout and midpoint controls
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed calibration: within each developmental stage and relevant wounded epidermal context, apply a bounded calibration pulse and independently verify cessation of the intracellular input at washout time t_w; removal of an external reagent alone is insufficient. With S=0 after t_w, predict R(t_w+τ)=R(t_w)exp(−λ_sτ). Multiple post-washout readings test log-linearity and estimate λ_s separately rather than imposing a common rate. If a known constant intracellular input S₀ can also be established for duration d, estimate gain from k_s=λ_s[R(t_w+d)−exp(−λ_s d)R(t_w)]/[S₀(1−exp(−λ_s d))], with t_w here denoting the start of that calibration pulse. Include sham delivery, imaging-only, baseline-drift, viability and wound-closure controls. Randomize animals within clutch and stage, mask analysis, and propagate calibration uncertainty at the animal/clutch level rather than treating cells or frames as independent replicates. These controls are proposed, not performed or established feasible.

review.rationale: Verified zero input predicts exponential decay, and the constant-input state-transition formula rearranges to the proposed gain estimate. Separate stage/context calibration avoids assuming stage-invariant kinetics. The step correctly labels feasibility, controls and uncertainty propagation as prospective rather than performed.

reasoning_steps.title: Limit the additional measurement claim
reasoning_steps.argument: One midpoint separates A and B, not all possible inputs. Equal reporter states at that sample then preserve every subsequent reading under identical subsequent inputs. Continuous noiseless R(t), together with valid kinetics, would recover S(t)=[dR/dt+λ_sR(t)]/k_s almost everywhere. Real differentiation amplifies measurement noise, so practical persistence inference needs a validated temporal bandwidth or rate bound, uncertainty-aware reconstruction and a stated minimum detectable gap; finite readings alone do not establish uninterrupted signaling.

review.rationale: Within an unsampled interval, replacing constant positive input with an appropriately amplified terminal pulse can preserve the next sampled state and all later states under identical subsequent input. reasoning_steps.title: Preserve the useful analytical constraints without transferring them to GEO
reasoning_steps.argument: The cycle-1 extract gives the conditional unpaired-data result: for binary early and late states with marginals p and q, their joint probability r can range from max(0,p+q−1) to min(p,q), while covariance is r−pq. Thus nondegenerate unpaired marginals do not identify within-animal coupling; at degenerate marginals covariance is zero, but substantive coupling cannot be learned from absent variation. The cycle-2 extract gives a separate conditional measurement counterexample under dR/dt=kS−λR: constant input and an early-input/gap/late-pulse trajectory match readings at 0.5 and 3 hours when the late amplitude is (1−exp(−2.5λ))/(1−exp(−0.5λ)). Their intervening signals differ. These constraints block treating unpaired means or two reporter readings as established animal-level persistence. Neither establishes actual GEO sampling or an actual reporter's validity.

The proposed direction is a positive persistence-by-refractory-stage interaction, with later RIC entry measured around 6 hours; these timings are prospective, not verified dataset coverage. A calibrated longitudinal readout and experimentally achieved waveform controls would be needed to distinguish this dependency from reporter kinetics, total exposure, composition or a signal-insensitive RIC-entry defect. A verified persistence increase without a precisely excluded minimum useful RIC/regeneration benefit would count against the candidate; failure to change persistence would not. No such observation exists in the supplied evidence, and later recovery remains outside the tested scope.

artifacts.claim_or_question: Under the explicitly restricted linear models below, two pulse times crossed with two post-pulse delays can distinguish shortened signal memory from pulse-time-only inducibility; an overlapping absolute readout time additionally tests readout-time-only wound-clock gating. reasoning_steps.title: Preserve prior limitations and delimit the evidence
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied bounded extract of artifact 108bd13c-d94e-4d8f-8da2-5e7f52cf2958 contains the opposite-coupling construction for unpaired marginals and the stage-summary rank identity SX=x46 S. Both remain valid mathematical constraints, not evidence about actual GEO pairing. Its single-terminal-time memory model is a candidate, not a certified biological premise. The present derivation addresses its unresolved memory/gain and exposure ambiguities. The original artifact and the underlying GEO records/publications have not been inspected.

reasoning_steps.title: Define input, memory signal and two distinct outputs
reasoning_steps.argument: Let s denote developmental stage, p pulse onset, d elapsed time after onset, and t=p+d absolute wound age. Let u_p(t) be the perturbation-induced effective intracellular input in basal epidermis, with support p to p+w. Define the actual intervening signal P by P'=b_s u_p-k_s P, with zero incremental initial state. Let N be instantaneous nascent transcription and R an accumulated readout satisfying R'=N-lambda_s R. All quantities are perturbation-minus-time-matched-control responses under linear superposition. P, intracellular ROS input and an accumulated fluorescent reporter are not interchangeable. The derivations require positive responses, constant coefficients in the tested window, no saturation, no unmodeled feedback or hidden parallel memory, and sufficiently resolved assay calibration.

reasoning_steps.title: State the competing models and indispensable restrictions
reasoning_steps.argument: Memory model M has stage-dependent k_s and N=q_s P, with q_s independent of both pulse time and wound age. Input-gate model GI has common decay k0, but may change the encoded pulse amplitude C_s(p); after pulse termination N=q_s C_s(p) exp(-k0 d). Its gate cannot continue creating an unmeasured input after washout. Output-gate model GO has common decay k0, pulse-time-independent encoded amplitude C_s, and N=q_s g_s(t) C_s exp(-k0 d), where g_s is a function only of absolute wound age, not of pulse history. Turnover model T has common signal decay k0 and constant transcriptional gain, but stage-dependent lambda_s. These are distinct restricted alternatives. Allowing arbitrary pulse-history dependence, hidden states, or simultaneous unrestricted encoding and output gates removes the intended identification.

reasoning_steps.title: A crossed schedule with an informative shared wound age
reasoning_steps.argument: Choose p2-p1=d2-d1=L>0 and d1>w. Then t12=p1+d2 equals t21=p2+d1. One illustrative schedule retaining the previous pulse times is p1=0.5, p2=4, d1=2 and d2=5.5 hours: the four readouts occur at 2.5, 6, 6 and 9.5 hpa. These are design values, not verified biological windows. Each animal receives only its assigned pulse; terminal assays use separate randomized animals for each cell of the design. Under matched translated inputs, integration gives P_s(p+d)=C_s exp(-k_s d), where C_s=b_s integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv. The same C_s applies to both pulse times within stage only if input profiles and encoding gain satisfy the stated restrictions.

reasoning_steps.title: Distinguish memory from the original pulse-time-gain alternative
reasoning_steps.argument: Write N_sij=N_s(p_i+d_j). Under M, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k_s L for either pulse time, and N_s2j/N_s1j=1 at either common delay. Under GI, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k0 L, while N_s2j/N_s1j=C_s(p2)/C_s(p1). Thus GI can mimic a stage-dependent late/early pulse response at one terminal time but cannot mimic unequal stage-specific delay slopes over the crossed design when its post-pulse memory is common. This follows by cancellation of pulse-specific amplitudes within each pulse arm. Equal k_s, constant input gates or insufficient precision are nondiscriminating cases, not evidence favoring one mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: Distinguish output-clock gating and explain why overlap matters
reasoning_steps.argument: Under GO, N_sij=q_s C_s g_s(p_i+d_j) exp(-k0 d_j). If all four absolute times are distinct, an unrestricted positive g_s can interpolate the four values required to mimic M; crossing alone is insufficient. At the shared time t12=t21, however, g_s cancels: K_s=log(N_s21/N_s12)/L=k0. Under M, K_s=k_s. Consequently K46-K40>0 is predicted by shortened stage-46 memory, whereas GO with common memory predicts zero. A pulse-time encoding gate does not cancel at this shared time, which is why the within-pulse delay contrasts from the previous step are also needed. The overlap result requires equal encoded amplitudes across pulse times under GO.

reasoning_steps.title: Exhibit the remaining unrestricted-gating equivalence
reasoning_steps.argument: Even the crossed design is not a universal identification theorem. For impulse responses, a common-memory model N=a_s(p)g_s(t) exp(-k0 d) reproduces M exactly by choosing a_s(p)=q_s C_s exp[(k_s-k0)p] and g_s(t)=exp[-(k_s-k0)t]. Their product is q_s C_s exp(-k_s d). This equality holds for every p and d, not merely four measurements. Therefore output-only observations cannot exclude combined encoding and wound-clock gates. Measuring the actual causal P, rather than an upstream correlate, supplies an additional restriction: common-memory alternatives predict a common normalized post-pulse P decay, whereas M predicts stage-specific decay. Without validating that P is the relevant intervening state, this broader biological ambiguity remains.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove the memory-versus-turnover ambiguity
reasoning_steps.argument: For an ideal impulse producing P=C exp(-k d), zero initial R and N=qP, integration gives R(d)=qC[exp(-k d)-exp(-lambda d)]/(lambda-k). At lambda=k the continuous limit is qC d exp(-k d). The expression is invariant under exchanging k and lambda. More generally, for any finite input the zero-state response is bq times the convolution of u, exp(-k t) and exp(-lambda t); convolution commutes. Thus a model with stage-dependent k_s and common lambda0 has exactly the same R as a model with common k0=lambda0 and stage-dependent lambda_s=k_s, with matched gain products. No number of accumulated-output observations alone breaks this equivalence under these linear models.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify what a validated proximal trajectory actually identifies
reasoning_steps.argument: After verified washout, a calibrated P trajectory identifies k_s from -d log(P)/dt, independent of a constant unknown amplitude. M requires the same within-stage decay for both pulse times, faster decay at stage 46, and constant N/P=q_s across wound ages. GI permits pulse-amplitude differences but requires common normalized decay. GO requires common normalized decay and N/P varying only with wound age. T requires common P decay and constant N/P; its apparent output persistence differs through lambda_s. Direct nascent N avoids accumulated-output turnover. Alternatively, with independently measured lambda_s and adequately resolved R, N=R'+lambda_s R. Four accumulated-output endpoints do not supply a nonparametric derivative or calibrate arbitrary reporter kinetics. A sensor trajectory with unknown stage-dependent filtering is not a validated P trajectory.

reasoning_steps.title: Replace ROS-area matching with the required profile control
reasoning_steps.argument: The effective post-pulse signal is b_s exp(-k_s d) integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv, not a function of unweighted area alone. For an exact finite-pulse counterexample, give both inputs area A: u1=A/epsilon on [0,epsilon] and u2=A/epsilon on [w-epsilon,w], with 0<epsilon<w. Their weighted integrals differ by exp[k_s(w-epsilon)], despite equal area. The appropriate robust control is the same translated intracellular effective-input profile u_s,i(p_i+v,x)=u*(v,x), including amplitude, duration, rise/fall shape and relevant subcellular localization x. This matches the input, not the downstream P tail whose decay is being tested. Increment matching is sufficient only after testing additive superposition against endogenous injury signaling; otherwise relevant total input and initial-state differences must be controlled or explicitly modeled.

reasoning_steps.title: Bound profile mismatch and define the falsification contrast
reasoning_steps.argument: For a nonnegative kernel, if each achieved input lies pointwise between (1-epsilon)u* and (1+epsilon)u*, its linear response satisfies the same relative bounds. A log ratio of two responses can therefore be displaced by at most log[(1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon)], and a difference of two such log ratios by at most twice that amount. This is a theoretical tolerance bound, not measured uncertainty. At the shared wound age define D=log(N_46,21/N_46,12)-log(N_40,21/N_40,12). M gives D=L(k46-k40); GO and constant-gain common-memory T give D=0. GI may give positive D, but predicts common delay slopes. The previously proposed D≥log(1.5), approximately 0.405, remains only a minimum-effect design target. Nonpositive control-subtracted means invalidate these log contrasts; no pseudocount rescue is justified.

reasoning_steps.title: Bound the next biological test and its stopping rules
reasoning_steps.argument: First perform a separate feasibility pilot to validate a nonperturbing basal-epidermal input sensor, the candidate P assay, intracellular washout, nascent-transcription timing and any accumulated-readout turnover. Freeze the pulse protocol, profile tolerances and one primary contrast before confirmation. Randomize animals within stage and clutch across the four pulse/delay cells, timing-matched vehicles, sham delivery and injury-only controls; distribute allocation across days and mask scoring. Measure cell counts, tissue damage and wound closure to detect composition or toxicity effects. Estimate contrasts using animals as units and clutch/day structure, with simultaneous uncertainty for the small prespecified contrast family. Stop as mechanistically inconclusive if profile control, washout, assay calibration or model restrictions fail. Reject the designated minimum-effect version if its uncertainty upper bound falls below the threshold after exposure uncertainty is incorporated. Common P decay with valid measurement contradicts this specified P-memory hypothesis, not every possible hidden-memory mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: Assess peer extracts, novelty and the developmental scope
reasoning_steps.argument: Peer extracts 93746d61-5dd5-4709-9fa5-17294ac400f8 and a4378486-799b-4acd-9991-15fbf7e443f5 raise input matching and reporter-memory ambiguities; fc219f96-452e-4d88-be65-8983613199be records a source-readiness stop. These are unverified, partly truncated extracts, not inspected originals or independent confirmations. I adopt their calibration concerns as design constraints, not their unsupplied results as premises. They do not refute this restricted derivation. The proposed biological extension is that a verified post-refractory competent cohort should recover longer P persistence and reduced timing sensitivity; that is an additional conjecture, not entailed by comparing stages 40 and 46. No transfer from X. tropicalis is made. Novelty, animal-level prediction and functional relevance remain unassessed.

reasoning_steps.title: Define input, memory signal and two distinct outputs
reasoning_steps.argument: Let s denote developmental stage, p pulse onset, d elapsed time after onset, and t=p+d absolute wound age. Let u_p(t) be the perturbation-induced effective intracellular input in basal epidermis, with support p to p+w. Define the actual intervening signal P by P'=b_s u_p-k_s P, with zero incremental initial state. Let N be instantaneous nascent transcription and R an accumulated readout satisfying R'=N-lambda_s R. All quantities are perturbation-minus-time-matched-control responses under linear superposition. P, intracellular ROS input and an accumulated fluorescent reporter are not interchangeable. The derivations require positive responses, constant coefficients in the tested window, no saturation, no unmodeled feedback or hidden parallel memory, and sufficiently resolved assay calibration.

review.rationale: These are explicit premises for the conditional claim. Separating effective input, intervening state, nascent output and accumulated output is necessary; zero incremental state and linear superposition justify the subsequent response equations.

reasoning_steps.title: State the competing models and indispensable restrictions
reasoning_steps.argument: Memory model M has stage-dependent k_s and N=q_s P, with q_s independent of both pulse time and wound age. Input-gate model GI has common decay k0, but may change the encoded pulse amplitude C_s(p); after pulse termination N=q_s C_s(p) exp(-k0 d). Its gate cannot continue creating an unmeasured input after washout. Output-gate model GO has common decay k0, pulse-time-independent encoded amplitude C_s, and N=q_s g_s(t) C_s exp(-k0 d), where g_s is a function only of absolute wound age, not of pulse history. Turnover model T has common signal decay k0 and constant transcriptional gain, but stage-dependent lambda_s. These are distinct restricted alternatives. Allowing arbitrary pulse-history dependence, hidden states, or simultaneous unrestricted encoding and output gates removes the intended identification.

review.rationale: The restrictions define genuinely different model classes. Constant post-washout decay under GI, pulse-independent encoding under GO, and turnover-only variation under T are exactly the restrictions needed for the later cancellations.

reasoning_steps.title: A crossed schedule with an informative shared wound age
reasoning_steps.argument: Choose p2-p1=d2-d1=L>0 and d1>w. Then t12=p1+d2 equals t21=p2+d1. One illustrative schedule retaining the previous pulse times is p1=0.5, p2=4, d1=2 and d2=5.5 hours: the four readouts occur at 2.5, 6, 6 and 9.5 hpa. These are design values, not verified biological windows. Each animal receives only its assigned pulse; terminal assays use separate randomized animals for each cell of the design. Under matched translated inputs, integration gives P_s(p+d)=C_s exp(-k_s d), where C_s=b_s integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv. The same C_s applies to both pulse times within stage only if input profiles and encoding gain satisfy the stated restrictions.

review.rationale: The schedule gives 2.5, 6, 6 and 9.5 hpa, with both readout delays after pulse termination. Solving the linear state equation gives b_s exp(-k_s d) times the stated weighted input integral.

reasoning_steps.title: Distinguish memory from the original pulse-time-gain alternative
reasoning_steps.argument: Write N_sij=N_s(p_i+d_j). Under M, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k_s L for either pulse time, and N_s2j/N_s1j=1 at either common delay. Under GI, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k0 L, while N_s2j/N_s1j=C_s(p2)/C_s(p1). Thus GI can mimic a stage-dependent late/early pulse response at one terminal time but cannot mimic unequal stage-specific delay slopes over the crossed design when its post-pulse memory is common. This follows by cancellation of pulse-specific amplitudes within each pulse arm. Equal k_s, constant input gates or insufficient precision are nondiscriminating cases, not evidence favoring one mechanism.

review.rationale: Within a pulse arm, the encoded amplitude cancels between delays. M therefore gives slope -k_s and GI gives -k0; at equal delay, M is pulse-time invariant under its matched-input and constant-encoding premises.

reasoning_steps.title: Distinguish output-clock gating and explain why overlap matters
reasoning_steps.argument: Under GO, N_sij=q_s C_s g_s(p_i+d_j) exp(-k0 d_j). If all four absolute times are distinct, an unrestricted positive g_s can interpolate the four values required to mimic M; crossing alone is insufficient. At the shared time t12=t21, however, g_s cancels: K_s=log(N_s21/N_s12)/L=k0. Under M, K_s=k_s. Consequently K46-K40>0 is predicted by shortened stage-46 memory, whereas GO with common memory predicts zero. A pulse-time encoding gate does not cancel at this shared time, which is why the within-pulse delay contrasts from the previous step are also needed. The overlap result requires equal encoded amplitudes across pulse times under GO.

review.rationale: At t12=t21, GO's identical wound-age gain cancels, leaving log(N21/N12)=k0 L. M instead gives k_s L. Without overlap, unrestricted positive gate values can fit the four separate times.

reasoning_steps.title: Exhibit the remaining unrestricted-gating equivalence
reasoning_steps.argument: Even the crossed design is not a universal identification theorem. For impulse responses, a common-memory model N=a_s(p)g_s(t) exp(-k0 d) reproduces M exactly by choosing a_s(p)=q_s C_s exp[(k_s-k0)p] and g_s(t)=exp[-(k_s-k0)t]. Their product is q_s C_s exp(-k_s d). This equality holds for every p and d, not merely four measurements. Therefore output-only observations cannot exclude combined encoding and wound-clock gates. Measuring the actual causal P, rather than an upstream correlate, supplies an additional restriction: common-memory alternatives predict a common normalized post-pulse P decay, whereas M predicts stage-specific decay. Without validating that P is the relevant intervening state, this broader biological ambiguity remains.

review.rationale: Direct substitution gives exp[(k_s-k0)p] exp[-(k_s-k0)(p+d)] exp(-k0 d)=exp(-k_s d). Thus combined gates exactly reproduce M, and output-only observations cannot exclude that alternative.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove the memory-versus-turnover ambiguity
reasoning_steps.argument: For an ideal impulse producing P=C exp(-k d), zero initial R and N=qP, integration gives R(d)=qC[exp(-k d)-exp(-lambda d)]/(lambda-k). At lambda=k the continuous limit is qC d exp(-k d). The expression is invariant under exchanging k and lambda. More generally, for any finite input the zero-state response is bq times the convolution of u, exp(-k t) and exp(-lambda t); convolution commutes. Thus a model with stage-dependent k_s and common lambda0 has exactly the same R as a model with common k0=lambda0 and stage-dependent lambda_s=k_s, with matched gain products. No number of accumulated-output observations alone breaks this equivalence under these linear models.

review.rationale: Integrating R'=qC exp(-kd)-lambda R yields the displayed difference of exponentials, with the stated equal-rate limit. Exchanging k and lambda changes both numerator and denominator signs; convolution commutativity establishes the finite-input extension.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify what a validated proximal trajectory actually identifies
reasoning_steps.argument: After verified washout, a calibrated P trajectory identifies k_s from -d log(P)/dt, independent of a constant unknown amplitude. M requires the same within-stage decay for both pulse times, faster decay at stage 46, and constant N/P=q_s across wound ages. GI permits pulse-amplitude differences but requires common normalized decay. GO requires common normalized decay and N/P varying only with wound age. T requires common P decay and constant N/P; its apparent output persistence differs through lambda_s. Direct nascent N avoids accumulated-output turnover. Alternatively, with independently measured lambda_s and adequately resolved R, N=R'+lambda_s R. Four accumulated-output endpoints do not supply a nonparametric derivative or calibrate arbitrary reporter kinetics. A sensor trajectory with unknown stage-dependent filtering is not a validated P trajectory.

review.rationale: For the actual post-washout state obeying P'=-k_sP, its log derivative identifies k_s regardless of constant gain. N/P then tests the stipulated gain behavior. Recovering N from accumulated output requires calibrated lambda and temporal resolution, not merely four endpoints.

reasoning_steps.title: Replace ROS-area matching with the required profile control
reasoning_steps.argument: The effective post-pulse signal is b_s exp(-k_s d) integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv, not a function of unweighted area alone. For an exact finite-pulse counterexample, give both inputs area A: u1=A/epsilon on [0,epsilon] and u2=A/epsilon on [w-epsilon,w], with 0<epsilon<w. Their weighted integrals differ by exp[k_s(w-epsilon)], despite equal area. The appropriate robust control is the same translated intracellular effective-input profile u_s,i(p_i+v,x)=u*(v,x), including amplitude, duration, rise/fall shape and relevant subcellular localization x. This matches the input, not the downstream P tail whose decay is being tested. Increment matching is sufficient only after testing additive superposition against endogenous injury signaling; otherwise relevant total input and initial-state differences must be controlled or explicitly modeled.

review.rationale: Shifting the same rectangular exposure from the beginning to the end of the pulse window multiplies its exponentially weighted integral by exp[k_s(w-epsilon)]. Equal area is therefore insufficient, whereas translated effective-input profiles control this source of variation under superposition.

reasoning_steps.title: Bound profile mismatch and define the falsification contrast
reasoning_steps.argument: For a nonnegative kernel, if each achieved input lies pointwise between (1-epsilon)u* and (1+epsilon)u*, its linear response satisfies the same relative bounds. A log ratio of two responses can therefore be displaced by at most log[(1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon)], and a difference of two such log ratios by at most twice that amount. This is a theoretical tolerance bound, not measured uncertainty. At the shared wound age define D=log(N_46,21/N_46,12)-log(N_40,21/N_40,12). M gives D=L(k46-k40); GO and constant-gain common-memory T give D=0. GI may give positive D, but predicts common delay slopes. The previously proposed D≥log(1.5), approximately 0.405, remains only a minimum-effect design target. Nonpositive control-subtracted means invalidate these log contrasts; no pseudocount rescue is justified.

review.rationale: For 0<=epsilon<1 and a fixed nonnegative response kernel, pointwise input bounds propagate to response bounds. Two response factors bound a log ratio, and four bound its stage difference. The D formula follows from the shared-clock cancellation; it remains a proposed contrast, not an estimate.

Randomize animals within stage and clutch across the four pulse/delay cells, timing-matched vehicles, sham delivery and injury-only controls; distribute allocation across days and mask scoring. Measure cell counts, tissue damage and wound closure to detect composition or toxicity effects. Estimate contrasts using animals as units and clutch/day structure, with simultaneous uncertainty for the small prespecified contrast family. Stop as mechanistically inconclusive if profile control, washout, assay calibration or model restrictions fail. Reject the designated minimum-effect version if its uncertainty upper bound falls below the threshold after exposure uncertainty is incorporated. Common P decay with valid measurement contradicts this specified P-memory hypothesis, not every possible hidden-memory mechanism.

Allowing arbitrary pulse-history dependence, hidden states, or simultaneous unrestricted encoding and output gates removes the intended identification.

review.rationale: The restrictions define genuinely different model classes. Constant post-washout decay under GI, pulse-independent encoding under GO, and turnover-only variation under T are exactly the restrictions needed for the later cancellations.

argument_steps.title: A crossed schedule with an informative shared wound age
argument_steps.argument: Choose p2-p1=d2-d1=L>0 and d1>w. Then t12=p1+d2 equals t21=p2+d1. One illustrative schedule retaining the previous pulse times is p1=0.5, p2=4, d1=2 and d2=5.5 hours: the four readouts occur at 2.5, 6, 6 and 9.5 hpa. These are design values, not verified biological windows. Each animal receives only its assigned pulse; terminal assays use separate randomized animals for each cell of the design. Under matched translated inputs, integration gives P_s(p+d)=C_s exp(-k_s d), where C_s=b_s integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv. The same C_s applies to both pulse times within stage only if input profiles and encoding gain satisfy the stated restrictions.

review.rationale: The schedule gives 2.5, 6, 6 and 9.5 hpa, with both readout delays after pulse termination. Solving the linear state equation gives b_s exp(-k_s d) times the stated weighted input integral.

argument_steps.title: Distinguish memory from the original pulse-time-gain alternative
argument_steps.argument: Write N_sij=N_s(p_i+d_j). Under M, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k_s L for either pulse time, and N_s2j/N_s1j=1 at either common delay. Under GI, log(N_si2/N_si1)=-k0 L, while N_s2j/N_s1j=C_s(p2)/C_s(p1). Thus GI can mimic a stage-dependent late/early pulse response at one terminal time but cannot mimic unequal stage-specific delay slopes over the crossed design when its post-pulse memory is common. This follows by cancellation of pulse-specific amplitudes within each pulse arm. Equal k_s, constant input gates or insufficient precision are nondiscriminating cases, not evidence favoring one mechanism.

review.rationale: Within a pulse arm, the encoded amplitude cancels between delays. M therefore gives slope -k_s and GI gives -k0; at equal delay, M is pulse-time invariant under its matched-input and constant-encoding premises.

argument_steps.title: Distinguish output-clock gating and explain why overlap matters
argument_steps.argument: Under GO, N_sij=q_s C_s g_s(p_i+d_j) exp(-k0 d_j). If all four absolute times are distinct, an unrestricted positive g_s can interpolate the four values required to mimic M; crossing alone is insufficient. At the shared time t12=t21, however, g_s cancels: K_s=log(N_s21/N_s12)/L=k0. Under M, K_s=k_s. Consequently K46-K40>0 is predicted by shortened stage-46 memory, whereas GO with common memory predicts zero. A pulse-time encoding gate does not cancel at this shared time, which is why the within-pulse delay contrasts from the previous step are also needed. The overlap result requires equal encoded amplitudes across pulse times under GO.

review.rationale: At t12=t21, GO's identical wound-age gain cancels, leaving log(N21/N12)=k0 L. M instead gives k_s L. Without overlap, unrestricted positive gate values can fit the four separate times.

argument_steps.title: Exhibit the remaining unrestricted-gating equivalence
argument_steps.argument: Even the crossed design is not a universal identification theorem. For impulse responses, a common-memory model N=a_s(p)g_s(t) exp(-k0 d) reproduces M exactly by choosing a_s(p)=q_s C_s exp[(k_s-k0)p] and g_s(t)=exp[-(k_s-k0)t]. Their product is q_s C_s exp(-k_s d). This equality holds for every p and d, not merely four measurements. Therefore output-only observations cannot exclude combined encoding and wound-clock gates. Measuring the actual causal P, rather than an upstream correlate, supplies an additional restriction: common-memory alternatives predict a common normalized post-pulse P decay, whereas M predicts stage-specific decay. Without validating that P is the relevant intervening state, this broader biological ambiguity remains.

review.rationale: Direct substitution gives exp[(k_s-k0)p] exp[-(k_s-k0)(p+d)] exp(-k0 d)=exp(-k_s d). Thus combined gates exactly reproduce M, and output-only observations cannot exclude that alternative.

argument_steps.title: Prove the memory-versus-turnover ambiguity
argument_steps.argument: For an ideal impulse producing P=C exp(-k d), zero initial R and N=qP, integration gives R(d)=qC[exp(-k d)-exp(-lambda d)]/(lambda-k). At lambda=k the continuous limit is qC d exp(-k d). The expression is invariant under exchanging k and lambda. More generally, for any finite input the zero-state response is bq times the convolution of u, exp(-k t) and exp(-lambda t); convolution commutes. Thus a model with stage-dependent k_s and common lambda0 has exactly the same R as a model with common k0=lambda0 and stage-dependent lambda_s=k_s, with matched gain products. No number of accumulated-output observations alone breaks this equivalence under these linear models.

review.rationale: Integrating R'=qC exp(-kd)-lambda R yields the displayed difference of exponentials, with the stated equal-rate limit. Exchanging k and lambda changes both numerator and denominator signs; convolution commutativity establishes the finite-input extension.

argument_steps.title: Specify what a validated proximal trajectory actually identifies
argument_steps.argument: After verified washout, a calibrated P trajectory identifies k_s from -d log(P)/dt, independent of a constant unknown amplitude. M requires the same within-stage decay for both pulse times, faster decay at stage 46, and constant N/P=q_s across wound ages. GI permits pulse-amplitude differences but requires common normalized decay. GO requires common normalized decay and N/P varying only with wound age. T requires common P decay and constant N/P; its apparent output persistence differs through lambda_s. Direct nascent N avoids accumulated-output turnover. Alternatively, with independently measured lambda_s and adequately resolved R, N=R'+lambda_s R. Four accumulated-output endpoints do not supply a nonparametric derivative or calibrate arbitrary reporter kinetics. A sensor trajectory with unknown stage-dependent filtering is not a validated P trajectory.

review.rationale: For the actual post-washout state obeying P'=-k_sP, its log derivative identifies k_s regardless of constant gain. N/P then tests the stipulated gain behavior. Recovering N from accumulated output requires calibrated lambda and temporal resolution, not merely four endpoints.

argument_steps.title: Replace ROS-area matching with the required profile control
argument_steps.argument: The effective post-pulse signal is b_s exp(-k_s d) integral_0^w exp(k_s v)u(v)dv, not a function of unweighted area alone. For an exact finite-pulse counterexample, give both inputs area A: u1=A/epsilon on [0,epsilon] and u2=A/epsilon on [w-epsilon,w], with 0<epsilon<w. Their weighted integrals differ by exp[k_s(w-epsilon)], despite equal area. The appropriate robust control is the same translated intracellular effective-input profile u_s,i(p_i+v,x)=u*(v,x), including amplitude, duration, rise/fall shape and relevant subcellular localization x. This matches the input, not the downstream P tail whose decay is being tested. Increment matching is sufficient only after testing additive superposition against endogenous injury signaling; otherwise relevant total input and initial-state differences must be controlled or explicitly modeled.

review.rationale: Shifting the same rectangular exposure from the beginning to the end of the pulse window multiplies its exponentially weighted integral by exp[k_s(w-epsilon)]. Equal area is therefore insufficient, whereas translated effective-input profiles control this source of variation under superposition.

argument_steps.title: Bound profile mismatch and define the falsification contrast
argument_steps.argument: For a nonnegative kernel, if each achieved input lies pointwise between (1-epsilon)u* and (1+epsilon)u*, its linear response satisfies the same relative bounds. A log ratio of two responses can therefore be displaced by at most log[(1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon)], and a difference of two such log ratios by at most twice that amount. This is a theoretical tolerance bound, not measured uncertainty. At the shared wound age define D=log(N_46,21/N_46,12)-log(N_40,21/N_40,12). M gives D=L(k46-k40); GO and constant-gain common-memory T give D=0. GI may give positive D, but predicts common delay slopes. The previously proposed D≥log(1.5), approximately 0.405, remains only a minimum-effect design target. Nonpositive control-subtracted means invalidate these log contrasts; no pseudocount rescue is justified.

review.rationale: For 0<=epsilon<1 and a fixed nonnegative response kernel, pointwise input bounds propagate to response bounds. Two response factors bound a log ratio, and four bound its stage difference. The D formula follows from the shared-clock cancellation; it remains a proposed contrast, not an estimate.

argument_steps.title: Bound the next biological test and its stopping rules
argument_steps.argument: First perform a separate feasibility pilot to validate a nonperturbing basal-epidermal input sensor, the candidate P assay, intracellular washout, nascent-transcription timing and any accumulated-readout turnover. Freeze the pulse protocol, profile tolerances and one primary contrast before confirmation. Randomize animals within stage and clutch across the four pulse/delay cells, timing-matched vehicles, sham delivery and injury-only controls; distribute allocation across days and mask scoring. Measure cell counts, tissue damage and wound closure to detect composition or toxicity effects. Estimate contrasts using animals as units and clutch/day structure, with simultaneous uncertainty for the small prespecified contrast family. Stop as mechanistically inconclusive if profile control, washout, assay calibration or model restrictions fail. Reject the designated minimum-effect version if its uncertainty upper bound falls below the threshold after exposure uncertainty is incorporated. Common P decay with valid measurement contradicts this specified P-memory hypothesis, not every possible hidden-memory mechanism.

review.rationale: The proposed allocation uses animals as units, treats clutch/day as nuisance structure, and distinguishes assay failure from falsification. Common validated P decay would contradict this specified P-memory hypothesis, while an upper bound below the chosen threshold would reject only the minimum-effect version.

The proposed biological extension is that a verified post-refractory competent cohort should recover longer P persistence and reduced timing sensitivity; that is an additional conjecture, not entailed by comparing stages 40 and 46. No transfer from X. tropicalis is made. Novelty, animal-level prediction and functional relevance remain unassessed.

review.rationale: The visible peer extracts justify retaining calibration and source-readiness concerns, not importing their omitted results. The recovery-stage statement is explicitly an additional conjecture, and no cross-species or novelty inference is asserted.

Stop this candidate branch without another algebraic extension. No measured effect size, uncertainty interval, held-out baseline improvement, novelty determination or independent confirmation is available. The prior analytical framework remains a conditional design contribution; it does not meet the scientific-success or computational-result criteria. Novelty and empirical generality are not assessed, and no explanation of loss followed by recovery of regeneration competence has been established.

review.rationale: The requested continuation gate explicitly required candidate and assay evidence or closure. objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 3 checks the feasibility premise left open in cycle 2 and finds no named P or validated measurement package in the supplied evidence. It identifies an appropriate future comparison of independently calibrated state decay but reports no observation. The resulting bounded conclusion is to stop this candidate pending new evidence while preserving the conditional identification framework and all biological, source-audit and validation obligations.

argument_steps.title: Separate supplied material from unavailable sources
argument_steps.argument: Artifact 574823c8-1e9c-4cdd-bac4-df6b24766570 is supplied as an incomplete extract and explicitly reports no identified P, validated assay, primary-source audit or biological measurement. Artifact 108bd13c-d94e-4d8f-8da2-5e7f52cf2958 is only a pointer in this packet; its original has not been inspected. The supplied ledger records the relevant feasibility obligations as unresolved. These facts establish the present evidence boundary, not what the unavailable original publications might contain.

review.rationale: The supplied extract explicitly reports missing molecular identification, assay validation, primary-source inspection and biological measurements. Artifact 108bd13c-d94e-4d8f-8da2-5e7f52cf2958 is pointer-only here, so limiting conclusions to the packet is justified.

argument_steps.title: The molecular-candidate and assay gate is unmet
argument_steps.argument: The available extract defines P by its proposed dynamical role, not by a molecular identity. It supplies no candidate-specific localization record, assay protocol, stage-specific calibration, intracellular washout trace or nonperturbation comparison. Consequently, I cannot supply an evidence-supported named basal-epidermal P with the requested assay. An upstream ROS measurement would measure input unless its distinct intervening role were demonstrated; a downstream transcriptional reporter would remain subject to reporter persistence. Renaming either as P would not satisfy the missing premise.

review.rationale: The visible cycle-2 equations specify P by function, not molecular identity. No candidate-specific protocol or calibration accompanies them. Measuring input ROS or accumulated transcription does not establish the intervening state without additional evidence.

argument_steps.title: Specify the separating result without claiming it occurred
argument_steps.argument: For any future named candidate, measurement kinetics must be calibrated independently within each stage and relevant injury context, rather than estimated freely from the same decay curves used to infer biological persistence. Continued effective intracellular input must also be measured or bounded independently. Common corrected P decay, supported by a prespecified equivalence interval and agreement with an orthogonal endogenous-state measurement, would favor the measurement-kinetics explanation over the specified faster-stage-46-P-decay hypothesis. Conversely, faster stage-46 decay that remains after propagating calibration and washout uncertainty and agrees with the orthogonal assay would support genuine stage-dependent decay of that candidate. A nonsignificant stage difference alone would establish neither equivalence nor common decay. Neither result has been observed here.

review.rationale: Independent stage-specific calibration and input-termination constraints prevent freely trading measurement kinetics against biological decay. An equivalence interval, rather than a nonsignificant difference, is needed to support common decay. The step appropriately describes prospective support between restricted alternatives, not universal identification.

argument_steps.title: A valid measurement would still not establish causal mediation
argument_steps.argument: Even a correctly measured stage-dependent trajectory could be a correlate rather than the state coupling injury to the RIC/ECM program. Functional mediation would require a candidate-specific perturbation that changes persistence while controlling achieved input, toxicity, cell composition and direct effects on the later program. Orthogonal terminal assays in separate animals could validate live measurements but could not alone establish longitudinal animal-level prediction. Cells and repeated images remain nested observations; animals are the biological units. Recovery of persistence after the refractory period remains a separate, untested prediction.

review.rationale: A stage-associated trajectory alone does not establish mediation. Controlling input, toxicity, composition and direct late effects is necessary for interpreting a persistence manipulation. Separate terminal animals cannot alone supply within-animal longitudinal prediction, and recovery-stage behavior is not entailed by a two-stage comparison.

argument_steps.title: Use peer extracts only as unresolved constraints
argument_steps.argument: The visible peer extracts flag reporter filtering, exposure matching and unavailable primary records. I adopt these as feasibility constraints, not as independently verified biological findings. The two-endpoint reporter claim in a4378486-799b-4acd-9991-15fbf7e443f5 concerns a restricted reporter model, not a measured Xenopus molecular trajectory; it cannot refute all candidate P mechanisms. The source-readiness stop in fc219f96-452e-4d88-be65-8983613199be is consistent with this packet's missing records but supplies no independent replication. Their truncated originals remain uninspected.

reasoning_steps.title: Preserve the useful analytical constraints without transferring them to GEO
reasoning_steps.argument: The cycle-1 extract gives the conditional unpaired-data result: for binary early and late states with marginals p and q, their joint probability r can range from max(0,p+q−1) to min(p,q), while covariance is r−pq. Thus nondegenerate unpaired marginals do not identify within-animal coupling; at degenerate marginals covariance is zero, but substantive coupling cannot be learned from absent variation. The cycle-2 extract gives a separate conditional measurement counterexample under dR/dt=kS−λR: constant input and an early-input/gap/late-pulse trajectory match readings at 0.5 and 3 hours when the late amplitude is (1−exp(−2.5λ))/(1−exp(−0.5λ)). Their intervening signals differ. These constraints block treating unpaired means or two reporter readings as established animal-level persistence. Neither establishes actual GEO sampling or an actual reporter's validity.

review.rationale: Cycle 1 supplies the four joint probabilities and their nonnegativity bounds. Cycle 2 supplies the positive-gain, positive-decay, calibrated first-order model and explicit nonnegative inputs whose weighted contributions coincide. These derivations support the restricted claims, including the correction for degenerate marginals.

reasoning_steps.title: Retain the candidate while identifying what would discriminate it
reasoning_steps.argument: The candidate is that, at comparable early injury-response magnitude, sustained basal-epidermal redox input during the first approximately 3 hours is more limiting for subsequent RIC entry in refractory than competent animals. The proposed direction is a positive persistence-by-refractory-stage interaction, with later RIC entry measured around 6 hours; these timings are prospective, not verified dataset coverage. A calibrated longitudinal readout and experimentally achieved waveform controls would be needed to distinguish this dependency from reporter kinetics, total exposure, composition or a signal-insensitive RIC-entry defect. A verified persistence increase without a precisely excluded minimum useful RIC/regeneration benefit would count against the candidate; failure to change persistence would not. No such observation exists in the supplied evidence, and later recovery remains outside the tested scope.

review.rationale: The candidate has a prospective direction, tissue and timing and is correctly separated from observations. However, its stated falsification sentence does not express the required uncertainty criterion.
